Simmer for 6 minutes until the noodles are tender.
Turn off the heat.
Stir in the perilla oil.
Adjust seasoning with salt to taste.
Garnish with chopped green onions.
notes: Use toasted perilla oil for a deeper nutty aroma
Rinse buckwheat noodles briefly in cold water before adding to the pot to remove excess starch if a clearer broth is preferred
Vegetable stock can replace the anchovy broth for a vegetarian option

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Tilapia with Fried Garlic and Shallots
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown fried tilapia fillet sits centered on a matte blue ceramic plate. The fish is whole and unsliced, featuring a craggy, crispy exterior. A mountain of golden-fried garlic bits and translucent, crispy shallot rings covers the top of the fish. Fresh green cilantro sprigs are tucked to the side. A small white bowl of jasmine rice and a tiny saucer of chili-fish sauce with sliced red bird's eye chilies sit nearby. The setting is a dark wood table with a folded linen napkin and traditional Thai brass spoon and fork. Lighting is natural and soft, highlighting the oily sheen of the aromatics and the texture of the crust. The entire plate is visible with balanced negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice in a separate bowl
Accompany with Prik Nam Pla (fish sauce with sliced chilies)
Eat using a spoon in the right hand and a fork in the left to push food onto the spoon
instructions: Pat tilapia fillets dry with paper towels.
Marinate fish with fish sauce and white pepper for 15 minutes.
Heat oil in a wok or deep pan to 160°C.
Fry shallot rings until golden and crisp. Remove and drain on paper towels.
Fry minced garlic in the same oil until light golden. Remove and drain immediately.
Increase oil temperature to 180°C.
Dredge tilapia fillets lightly in cornstarch. Shake off excess.
Fry fillets for 4 minutes per side until deep golden and crispy.
Drain fish on a wire rack.
Top each fillet with a generous amount of fried garlic and shallots.
Garnish with cilantro sprigs and serve with lime wedges.
notes: Ensure the garlic is removed from oil just before it turns dark brown to avoid bitterness.
The fish must be very dry before dredging to ensure maximum crunch.

recipes.recipe_name: Senegalese Chicken Maafe
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Maafe is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The focal point is a whole, bone-in chicken thigh, its skin deeply browned and glistening, nestled in a thick, velvety peanut sauce of a rich burnt-orange color. Large, softened chunks of orange sweet potato and thick carrot rounds are arranged naturally around the meat. The sauce shows a light sheen with tiny droplets of red oil. A neat, circular mound of steamed white long-grain rice sits on the side of the bowl. Garnish with a single whole red chili and a small sprig of fresh flat-leaf parsley. The scene is set on a dark wood table with a neutral cotton napkin and a traditional carved wooden spoon.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with white jasmine or basmati rice
Accompany with a side of spicy onion relish (Yassa style)
Traditionally eaten with the right hand if served communally
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden brown, about 5 minutes.
Flip chicken and sear for 3 minutes. Remove from pot and set aside.
Add onion to the pot. Sauté for 4 minutes until translucent.
Add garlic and ginger. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes while stirring constantly.
Whisk peanut butter into the chicken stock until smooth.
Pour the peanut stock mixture into the pot.
Add sweet potato chunks, carrot rounds, and the whole scotch bonnet pepper.
Return chicken to the pot. Submerge pieces in the liquid.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer covered for 30 minutes.
Check chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove the scotch bonnet pepper before serving.
Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
notes: Do not cut or pierce the scotch bonnet to keep the heat mild.
Use natural peanut butter without added sugar for authentic flavor.
The sauce should be thick enough to coat a spoon heavily.

recipes.recipe_name: Aloo Gajar Palak (Spiced Potato, Carrot, and Spinach)
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Aloo Gajar Palak served in a shallow, rustic ceramic bowl. The dish features 2cm cubes of tender yellow potatoes and 1cm rounds of bright orange carrots coated in a thick, savory tomato-based masala. Dark green, wilted spinach leaves are folded throughout, adding textural contrast. The vegetables appear moist but not swimming in liquid. The bowl sits on a dark, weathered wooden table. A simple, hand-woven cotton napkin lies beside the bowl. A small stainless steel spoon is placed to the right. The lighting is warm and soft, coming from the side to highlight the steam rising from the vegetables and the natural textures of the cooked ingredients.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm rotis or parathas
Accompany with a side of plain yogurt or raita
Provide a wedge of lemon for acidity

ingredients.name: potatoes, peeled and cut into 2cm cubes

instructions: Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add cumin seeds and bay leaf. Fry until seeds sizzle.
Add onion. Sauté 5 minutes until translucent.
Add garlic. Stir 1 minute.
Add potatoes and carrots. Stir to coat in oil.
Add chili powder, ground coriander, salt, and pepper.
Add tomatoes. Stir well.
Cover the pan. Reduce heat to low.
Cook 15 to 20 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Add spinach. Stir until wilted.
Remove bay leaf before serving.
notes: Do not add water; the vegetables cook in their own juices and the moisture from the tomatoes.
Adjust chili powder to preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Murgh Do Pyaza
recipes.visual_description: The dish features large, succulent chunks of bone-in chicken thighs nestled in a thick, vibrant reddish-brown gravy. The sauce is textured with finely melted onions and studded with large, tender-crisp translucent onion petals. Bright green fresh cilantro leaves are scattered across the top. The chicken is cooked to a moist, tender finish with a visible spice coating. The meal is served in a polished copper kadai placed on a clean white porcelain plate, providing a modern yet authentic touch. Beside the plate sits a stack of warm, charred garlic naan and a small bowl of cool cucumber raita. Natural lighting highlights the glossy sheen of the aromatic gravy and the rustic texture of the bread.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with hot garlic naan
Accompany with cucumber raita
Include a side of pickled red onions

ingredients.name: chicken thighs, bone-in, skinless, cut into large chunks

instructions: Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot.
Add cumin seeds, cardamom pods, and cinnamon stick.
Toast spices until fragrant.
Add diced onions.
Sauté until deep golden brown.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste.
Cook for 2 minutes.
Add turmeric, chili powder, and coriander powder.
Add chicken chunks.
Sear until browned on all sides.
Stir in tomato puree and whisked yogurt.
Cover the pot.
Simmer for 20 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Add onion petals.
Simmer 5 minutes until petals are tender-crisp.
Garnish with fresh cilantro.
notes: The name 'Do Pyaza' refers to onions being added at two different stages of the cooking process.
Use Kashmiri chili powder to achieve a vibrant red color without excessive heat.

recipes.recipe_name: Cuban-style Citrus Beef with Black Beans and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Cuban-style beef sits on a white porcelain plate. Three large beef chunks are placed on a bed of fluffy white rice. The beef has a dark brown, glazed surface. A portion of black beans is positioned next to the rice. Diced orange carrots are mixed with the beef. The plate has a clean arrangement with moderate negative space. Fresh orange zest and dried oregano are sprinkled on top. The plate rests on a light wooden table. A white cotton napkin and silver fork are placed to the side. Natural light highlights the texture of the meat chunks and the grains of rice. The background is a blurred bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fried plantains
Include a side of mojo sauce
instructions: Cut beef into 4cm chunks.
Season beef with salt, pepper, and oregano.
Heat oil in a heavy pot.
Sear beef chunks until browned.
Remove beef from pot.
Sauté diced onion and carrots for 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic.
Cook for 1 minute.
Return beef to pot.
Add orange juice, zest, and beef stock.
Simmer on low heat for 90 minutes.
Cook rice in 800ml water.
Heat black beans in a pan.
Place rice on plates.
Top with beef chunks and carrots.
Serve beans on the side.
notes: Use a heavy-bottomed pot for even braising.
Ensure beef is fork-tender before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Beef and Potato Tapas
recipes.visual_description: A rustic Spanish tapas presentation on a clean white porcelain plate. The base features golden, roasted potato cubes with crisp edges. Thick, seared beef chunks are nestled among the potatoes, showing a deep brown crust. Vibrant green beans, blanched and sautéed, are tucked between the beef and potatoes, adding a fresh vertical element. Sliced golden garlic chips and a light dusting of smoked paprika provide textural contrast and color. The dish is finished with a glossy drizzle of extra virgin olive oil. The setting is a modern bistro with a light oak table, a simple linen napkin, and even natural lighting that highlights the textures of the seared meat and roasted vegetables.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in traditional clay cazuelas
Accompany with crusty bread
Provide small wooden skewers for sharing
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Peel and cut potatoes into 2cm cubes.
Toss potatoes with 20ml olive oil and salt.
Roast potatoes on a baking tray for 25 minutes until golden.
Trim ends of green beans.
Boil beans in salted water for 3 minutes.
Transfer beans to ice water to stop cooking. Drain well.
Cut beef into 3cm chunks.
Season beef with salt and pepper.
Heat 20ml olive oil in a heavy skillet over high heat.
Sear beef chunks for 2 minutes per side for medium-rare.
Remove beef from pan and let rest for 5 minutes.
Heat remaining 40ml olive oil in the same pan over medium heat.
Fry garlic slices until light golden and crisp.
Add green beans and smoked paprika to the garlic oil.
Toss for 1 minute to coat and warm through.
Combine beef, potatoes, and beans on a serving platter.
notes: Ensure potatoes are completely dry before roasting for maximum crispness.
Do not crowd the pan when searing beef to maintain a high temperature.
Use high-quality Spanish smoked paprika for authentic flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato and Mushroom Spezzatino with Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rustic Italian stew is served in a shallow, cream-colored ceramic bowl. Thick 3cm chunks of tender potato and large, seared quarters of cremini mushrooms are coated in a glossy, savory reduction. Bright green broccoli florets are tucked between the potatoes, providing a color contrast. The arrangement is natural and unstudied, with ingredients overlapping. The bowl rests on a dark walnut table accompanied by a rustic piece of torn bread and a simple fork. Soft, warm kitchen lighting highlights the moisture on the vegetables and the steam. The background shows a hint of a salt cellar and a bottle of olive oil, creating a lived-in family atmosphere. The entire plate is visible, showcasing the hearty, home-cooked meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty rustic bread for scarpetta to mop up the sauce.
Drizzle with high-quality extra virgin olive oil at the table.
Pair with a glass of medium-bodied red wine such as Chianti.
instructions: Peel and cut potatoes into 3cm chunks.
Clean mushrooms and cut into quarters.
Cut broccoli into small florets.
Finely dice the onion and mince the garlic.
Heat olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat.
Sauté onion and garlic for 3 minutes.
Add mushrooms. Cook for 5 minutes until browned.
Add potatoes and rosemary sprig. Stir for 2 minutes.
Pour in broth until vegetables are half-submerged.
Simmer covered for 15 minutes.
Add broccoli florets. Cover and cook for 5 minutes.
Remove lid. Simmer for 2 minutes to thicken the sauce.
Season with salt and pepper.
notes: Use waxy potatoes like Yukon Gold to ensure they maintain their shape during braising.
Ensure mushrooms are well-browned before adding liquid to develop deep umami flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Earl Grey and Dragon Fruit Entremet with Activated Charcoal
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly smooth dome-shaped entremet sits centered on a matte white porcelain plate. The exterior is coated in a glossy, jet-black charcoal mirror glaze that reflects the light. On top of the dome, three small, precise cubes of vibrant pink dragon fruit are clustered to one side, providing a sharp color contrast. A single, small edible silver leaf flake rests near the fruit. The plate features significant negative space, emphasizing the dark, sleek pastry. The lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the reflective surface of the glaze and the matte texture of the dragon fruit. A modern stainless steel dessert spoon lies straight on the right side of the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve on a chilled white plate to maintain temperature
Pair with a light Earl Grey tea or a dry sparkling wine
Use a small dessert fork and spoon
instructions: Bloom 4g gelatin in cold water. Heat dragon fruit puree with 30g sugar. Stir in gelatin. Pour into small disc molds. Freeze until solid.
Whisk eggs, almond flour, powdered sugar, and 5g charcoal powder. Fold in melted butter. Spread on a baking sheet. Bake at 180°C for 10 minutes. Cool and cut into discs.
Bloom 6g gelatin. Heat milk with Earl Grey tea. Steep for 5 minutes. Strain. Pour hot milk over white chocolate. Stir until smooth. Add gelatin.
Fold whipped cream into the cooled Earl Grey chocolate base.
Place a small amount of mousse into silicone dome molds. Press a frozen dragon fruit disc into the center. Top with more mousse. Press a charcoal sponge disc on top. Freeze for 4 hours.
Mix neutral glaze with 5g charcoal powder. Heat to 35°C.
Unmold frozen entremets. Place on a wire rack. Pour charcoal glaze over each. Let excess drip off.
Transfer to plates. Garnish with fresh diced dragon fruit.
notes: Ensure the entremet is completely frozen before glazing for a smooth finish
Do not overheat the glaze or it will melt the mousse
Use high-quality food-grade activated charcoal

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Musakhan
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents two whole roasted chicken thighs with crisp, mahogany-colored skin, positioned centrally on a bed of soft, deep-purple caramelized onions. These rest on a circular, rustic Taboon flatbread that is stained gold with olive oil. The plating is clean and focused on a large white porcelain plate. Bright green chopped parsley and golden-brown toasted pine nuts are scattered generously over the chicken. The chicken skin shows visible grains of sumac and spices. Beside the plate sits a small, minimalist ceramic bowl of thick white yogurt. The background features a dark wood bistro table with a folded grey linen napkin and natural side lighting highlighting the textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of thick Greek yogurt or Labneh
Accompany with a simple Arabic salad of tomato and cucumber
Traditionally eaten by hand by tearing pieces of bread with the chicken
Provide extra lemon wedges for acidity
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss chicken thighs with 30ml olive oil, 1 tbsp sumac, cumin, cinnamon, allspice, salt, and pepper.
Place chicken on a baking sheet. Roast until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Heat remaining olive oil in a large pan over medium-low heat.
Add sliced onions and a pinch of salt. Sauté for 20 minutes until very soft.
Stir remaining 2 tbsp sumac into onions. Cook for 2 minutes until onions are deep purple.
Dip the edges of the flatbread into the sumac-infused onion oil.
Place bread on a baking tray. Spread a thick layer of sumac onions over the bread.
Place two roasted chicken thighs on top of the onions.
Bake for 5 minutes until the bread is warm and edges are slightly crisp.
Garnish with toasted pine nuts and fresh parsley.
notes: Use high-quality Palestinian olive oil for the most authentic flavor
Ensure onions are cooked slowly to avoid browning; they should be translucent and stained purple by the sumac
If Taboon bread is unavailable, use thick Greek-style pita or Naan

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Zucchini Boats with Spinach and Cheese Gratin
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion featuring two whole roasted zucchini boats placed parallel on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The zucchini boats exhibit a vibrant green skin and are topped with a bubbling, golden-brown gratin crust made of melted cheese and toasted bread crumbs. To the side, a fresh salad consists of 1cm cubes of bright red tomato and creamy green avocado, tossed with finely sliced red onion and halved black olives. The arrangement is clean and balanced, showing moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro with a light-colored wooden table, a folded white cotton napkin, and natural side-lighting that highlights the textures of the crispy gratin and the fresh, glistening vegetables.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crisp dry white wine
Accompany with crusty sourdough bread
Traditional Mediterranean family-style presentation
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Halve zucchini lengthwise. Scoop out the center flesh, leaving a 1cm shell.
Finely dice the scooped zucchini flesh, red onion, and garlic.
Sauté the diced vegetables in olive oil over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Add spinach to the pan. Cook until wilted. Drain all excess liquid thoroughly.
In a bowl, combine mayonnaise, mustard, cayenne pepper, half the cheese, and chopped black olives.
Fold the sautéed vegetable mixture into the mayonnaise base.
Fill the zucchini shells with the mixture. Place on a lined baking sheet.
Mix bread crumbs with the remaining cheese. Sprinkle over the filling.
Bake for 20 minutes until the zucchini is tender and the topping is golden brown.
Dice tomatoes and avocados into 1cm cubes. Season with salt and olive oil.
Serve two zucchini boats per plate with a side of the fresh avocado-tomato salad.
notes: Ensure spinach is squeezed dry to prevent the boats from becoming soggy.
Use a spoon to scoop zucchini to avoid piercing the outer skin.

recipes.recipe_name: Korean Braised Short Ribs (Galbi-jjim)
recipes.visual_description: The dish features thick, braised bone-in beef short ribs glazed in a dark, glossy mahogany sauce. The meat is tender and slightly pulled from the bone. Accompanying the ribs are large, turned chunks of daikon radish and carrots, cooked until translucent and saturated with braising liquid. Whole, plump shiitake mushrooms and firm chestnuts add textural variety. The ribs are piled naturally in a deep, matte-black ceramic bowl, leaving space for the rich, reduced sauce at the bottom. Finely sliced green onion rounds and toasted sesame seeds garnish the top. The setting includes a modern wooden table, a stainless steel bowl of steamed rice, and a small side of vibrant red kimchi. Natural side-lighting emphasizes the sauce’s sheen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed short-grain white rice
Include various banchan side dishes like kimchi and seasoned spinach
Provide stainless steel chopsticks and a long-handled spoon
Serve in a traditional stoneware jjim-yong-gi bowl
instructions: Soak beef ribs in cold water for 30 minutes. Drain and rinse.
Place ribs in a pot of boiling water. Boil for 5 minutes.
Drain ribs. Rinse under cold water. Trim excess fat.
Score the thickest parts of the meat with 2cm deep slits.
Mix soy sauce, sugar, mirin, pear, garlic, and ginger in a bowl.
Place ribs in a heavy pot. Pour sauce over meat. Add 500ml water.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 60 minutes.
Round the edges of radish and carrot chunks using a paring knife.
Add radish, carrots, mushrooms, and chestnuts to the pot.
Simmer covered for 30 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Remove lid. Increase heat to medium. Cook for 10 minutes to reduce sauce.
Skim fat from the surface of the liquid.
Stir in 1 tbsp of sesame oil.
Transfer ribs and vegetables to a deep serving bowl.
Garnish with green onions and sesame seeds.
notes: Rounding the vegetable edges prevents them from breaking during the long simmer.
The pear contains enzymes that naturally tenderize the tough rib meat.
Ensure ribs reach an internal temperature of 95°C for maximum tenderness.

recipes.recipe_name: Gluten-Free Carrot Gnocchi with Oregano Brown Butter
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of vibrant orange carrot gnocchi rests on a clean white porcelain plate. The gnocchi are cut into uniform 2cm pillows, showing a crisp, golden-brown sear from the pan. They are tossed in a glossy brown butter sauce flecked with toasted oregano leaves. The arrangement is natural and free-flowing, leaving ample negative space around the edges of the plate. Scattered over the top are thin, translucent shavings of Parmigiano-Reggiano and small, fresh oregano sprigs. The dish sits on a dark oak bistro table. A linen napkin and a heavy silver fork are placed to the side. The lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the contrast between the bright carrot and the deep herb tones.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a shallow warmed pasta bowl
Pair with a dry Italian white wine like Vermentino
Offer extra grated Parmigiano-Reggiano at the table
instructions: Peel carrots and cut into 2cm chunks.
Steam carrots until very tender.
Pass hot carrots through a ricer into a large bowl.
Spread carrot mash on a tray to cool and dry for 10 minutes.
Mix cooled mash with egg, parmesan, and salt.
Fold in gluten-free flour gradually to form a soft dough.
Roll dough into 2cm thick ropes on a floured surface.
Cut ropes into 2cm pillows.
Boil gnocchi in salted water until they float to the surface.
Remove gnocchi with a slotted spoon and drain.
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add garlic and oregano leaves to the butter.
Cook until butter turns golden brown and smells nutty.
Add gnocchi to the pan in a single layer.
Sear gnocchi for 2 minutes per side until crisp.
Season with black pepper and serve immediately.
notes: Ensure the carrot mash is as dry as possible before adding flour to maintain gnocchi structure.
Different gluten-free flour blends absorb moisture differently; add flour slowly until the dough is no longer sticky.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Salmon with Mirin-Soy Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single 150g whole salmon fillet sits on a clean white porcelain plate. The salmon is coated in a glossy, dark amber mirin-soy glaze that reflects light. Beside the fish, two vibrant green baby bok choy halves are neatly placed. The salmon is topped with a pinch of toasted white sesame seeds and bright green sliced onion rounds. The plate has moderate negative space for a clean, professional look. The background features a light-colored wooden table with a small bowl of steamed white rice and dark wooden chopsticks. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the flaky texture of the whole, unsliced fish and the viscous consistency of the glaze.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of short-grain steamed white rice
Accompany with pickled daikon or ginger
Provide high-quality wooden chopsticks for dining
instructions: Whisk soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar in a small bowl.
Pat salmon fillets dry with paper towels.
Heat sesame oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Place salmon in the pan skin-side down.
Sear for 4 minutes until skin is crispy.
Flip the salmon carefully.
Cook for another 2 minutes.
Remove salmon from the pan and set aside.
Add ginger and garlic to the same pan.
Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in the soy-mirin mixture.
Simmer for 3 minutes until the sauce thickens into a glaze.
Steam bok choy for 3 minutes until tender-crisp.
Return salmon to the pan briefly to coat with the glaze.
Serve immediately over rice.
notes: Do not overcook the salmon to maintain moisture.
Ensure the pan is hot before adding fish to achieve a crispy skin.
The glaze should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.

recipes.recipe_name: French Braised Leeks with Roasted Chicken Thighs
recipes.visual_description: A single portion served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl on a light oak bistro table. Two whole, roasted chicken thighs with crispy, dark golden-brown skin are positioned in the center. Surrounding the chicken are five 5cm cylindrical leek batons, showing deep caramelization on their flat ends and a soft, pale green interior. A glossy, light-amber mustard and white wine reduction pools at the base of the bowl, partially coating the leeks. Fine specks of bright green parsley are scattered over the top. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the contrast between the crispy chicken skin and the tender, translucent layers of the braised leeks. A white cotton napkin and silver flatware sit beside the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette to soak up the braising liquid
Pair with a chilled dry white wine such as Sauvignon Blanc or Chablis
Present in the cast iron skillet for family-style service

ingredients.name: large leeks (white and light green parts only)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Trim leeks and cut into 5cm cylindrical batons.
Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-proof skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down in the skillet.
Sear for 6 minutes until skin is golden and crisp.
Flip chicken and cook for 2 minutes. Remove chicken from pan.
Discard all but 15ml of fat from the pan.
Add butter to the skillet. Place leeks cut-side down in the butter.
Sear leeks for 3 minutes until ends are caramelized and brown.
Add garlic and thyme to the pan.
Pour in white wine. Scrape the bottom of the pan to release browned bits.
Reduce wine by half.
Stir Dijon mustard into the chicken stock and pour into the skillet.
Place chicken thighs on top of the leeks, skin-side up.
Transfer skillet to the oven. Roast for 20 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from oven. Let the dish rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure leeks are washed thoroughly between layers to remove grit
Do not cover the pan in the oven to keep the chicken skin crispy
Use a high-quality Dijon mustard for the best sauce emulsion

recipes.recipe_name: Potato and Tomato Salad with Hollandaise Dressing
recipes.visual_description: A large ceramic platter holds the salad on a well-worn wooden kitchen table. The base features a bed of roughly chopped, vibrant green romaine lettuce. On top, 1cm thick rounds of boiled potatoes are layered casually with bright red, thinly sliced tomato wedges. Delicate, translucent red onion rings are scattered across the vegetables. A creamy, pale yellow hollandaise sauce is drizzled in organic patterns, partially coating the potato rounds. The arrangement is natural and unpretentious, with ingredients overlapping. The scene is captured in warm, soft kitchen light, showing the entire plate. A simple linen napkin and a stainless steel fork rest beside the platter, creating a lived-in, authentic home dining atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm as a light lunch
Accompany with crusty baguette slices
instructions: Boil potatoes in salted water until tender.
Drain potatoes and let cool for 10 minutes.
Slice potatoes into 1 cm thick rounds.
Slice tomatoes into thin wedges.
Finely slice the red onion into thin rings.
Chop the lettuce into bite-sized pieces.
Whisk hollandaise sauce with lemon juice in a small bowl.
Place chopped lettuce on a large serving platter.
Arrange potato slices and tomato wedges over the lettuce.
Scatter onion rings across the top.
Drizzle the thinned hollandaise sauce over the vegetables.
Season with salt and pepper.
Garnish with chopped chives.
notes: Thin the hollandaise slightly more with warm water if it is too thick to drizzle.
Ensure potatoes are still slightly warm when adding the dressing to absorb the flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Gochujang Glazed Tempeh with Red Pepper Couscous
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Gochujang Glazed Tempeh with Red Pepper Couscous sits on a clean white porcelain plate. The hero ingredient, tempeh, is cut into 2cm cubes and seared until the edges are crisp. A thick, glossy dark-red gochujang glaze coats the cubes, reflecting light. The tempeh is arranged in a natural, slightly elevated mound atop a bed of fluffy couscous. The couscous is speckled with finely diced 5mm red pepper brunoise and minced green onions. Vibrant green scallion curls and white toasted sesame seeds garnish the top. The scene is set on a light oak table with a white cotton napkin and polished stainless steel cutlery. Soft natural side-lighting emphasizes the textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of baechu-kimchi
Accompany with chilled barley tea
instructions: Cut tempeh into 2cm cubes.
Finely dice red peppers into 5mm pieces.
Whisk gochujang, soy sauce, honey, sesame oil, garlic, and ginger in a small bowl.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear tempeh cubes until golden brown on all sides.
Pour gochujang mixture over tempeh.
Toss to coat and cook for 3 minutes until glaze thickens and sticks to the cubes.
Bring vegetable broth to a boil in a medium pot.
Stir in couscous and diced red peppers.
Cover, remove from heat, and let sit for 5 minutes.
Fluff couscous with a fork.
Divide couscous among four plates.
Top with glazed tempeh cubes.
Garnish with green onions and sesame seeds.
notes: Ensure the skillet is hot before adding tempeh to get a crisp exterior.
Do not overcook the glaze or the honey will burn.

recipes.recipe_name: Swiss Chard and Asparagus Risotto
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a wide, shallow, cream-colored ceramic bowl with a slightly irregular edge. The risotto has a fluid, all'onda consistency, spreading naturally across the plate surface rather than being mounded. Vibrant green blanched asparagus tips and bright green ribbons of wilted Swiss chard are distributed throughout the creamy, pale rice. Small, translucent diced chard stems add subtle texture. A light dusting of finely grated parmesan and bright yellow lemon zest covers the top. The plate rests on a dark, rustic wooden table next to a simple stainless steel fork and a folded linen napkin. Warm, soft kitchen lighting highlights the glossy, buttery sheen of the rice.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian sourdough bread
Pair with a crisp dry white wine like Pinot Grigio
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table
instructions: Heat vegetable stock in a pot. Maintain a low simmer.
Remove woody ends from asparagus. Cut stalks into 3cm batons. Keep tips whole.
Separate Swiss chard stems from leaves. Dice stems finely. Shred leaves into wide ribbons.
Heat olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat.
Sauté diced onion and chard stems for 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and asparagus batons. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add rice to the pan. Toast for 2 minutes until edges are translucent.
Add one ladle of hot stock. Stir constantly until liquid is absorbed.
Continue adding stock one ladle at a time. Stir frequently.
Stir in shredded chard leaves and asparagus tips when rice is nearly tender.
Cook until rice is al dente. Ensure the consistency is fluid and creamy.
Remove from heat. Stir in butter and grated parmesan for the mantecatura.
Add lemon zest. Season with salt and pepper. Serve immediately.
notes: Always use hot stock to maintain the cooking temperature of the rice
Stirring is essential to release the rice starches for a creamy texture
The risotto should move like a slow wave when the plate is tilted

recipes.recipe_name: Ancho and Malt Vinegar Braised Beef
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of braised beef is served on a clean, off-white stoneware plate. At the base, a smooth layer of warm refried beans provides a creamy foundation. Three substantial 5cm chunks of beef chuck, braised to a deep mahogany hue, are positioned centrally. The meat is coated in a glossy, thick sauce made from ancho chiles and smoked paprika. Bright red radish wedges and small diced white onions are scattered over the top for crunch. Fresh cilantro leaves add a pop of green. Two warm, hand-pressed corn tortillas rest in a small basket nearby. Natural light emphasizes the rich textures of the sauce and the rustic wooden table setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Accompany with fresh lime wedges
Provide pickled red onions as a side condiment

ingredients.name: dried ancho chiles, stems and seeds removed

instructions: Soak ancho chiles in hot water for 15 minutes. Blend into a smooth paste.
Pat beef chunks dry. Season with salt.
Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks in batches until browned. Remove beef from pot.
Add onion and garlic to the pot. Sauté for 3 minutes.
Stir in smoked paprika and ancho paste. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in malt vinegar. Scrape the bottom of the pot to deglaze.
Return beef to the pot. Add beef stock.
Simmer covered on low heat for 2 hours until meat is tender.
Heat refried beans in a separate saucepan until smooth.
Place a portion of beans on each plate. Top with beef chunks and sauce.
Garnish with radish wedges and cilantro.
notes: Ensure the beef is not shredded to maintain restaurant-quality presentation.
The malt vinegar provides a sharp contrast to the earthy ancho chiles.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish-Style Chicken and Tomato Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a whole bone-in chicken thigh with crispy, deeply browned skin resting atop a bed of fluffy, tomato-tinted rice. The rice displays a warm orange-red hue from the rendered tomato juices and contains visible softened tomato chunks and minced garlic. The plating is casual and hearty, presented on a rustic blue-rimmed ceramic plate. The chicken is centered but slightly offset, showcasing its textured, seared surface. A single sprig of parsley serves as a functional garnish. The scene is set on a dark wood table with a simple linen napkin and a stainless steel fork. Warm, natural light emphasizes the steam rising from the moist rice and the glistening chicken skin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty bread
Accompany with a simple green salad with lemon vinaigrette
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down. Sear until golden brown.
Flip chicken. Brown the other side. Remove chicken from pan.
Add minced garlic to the remaining fat. Sauté for 1 minute.
Stir in diced tomatoes. Cook until they soften and release juices.
Add rice to the pan. Stir to coat in the tomato mixture.
Pour in water. Add remaining salt. Stir once.
Place chicken back on top of the rice.
Cover with a lid. Reduce heat to low.
Simmer for 20 minutes until rice is tender and water is absorbed.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from heat. Let rest covered for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice while it simmers to ensure a fluffy texture.
Use chicken stock instead of water for deeper savory flavor.
Ensure the pan lid fits tightly to trap steam properly.

recipes.recipe_name: Asparagus and Pea Risotto with Fresh Herbs
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of vibrant green risotto served on a wide, flat white porcelain rimmed plate. The risotto has a fluid 'all'onda' consistency, spreading naturally across the plate without a ring mold. Bright green blanched asparagus tips, cut into 5cm lengths, are placed organically on top. Whole blanched peas are scattered throughout the rice. Fine ribbons of fresh mint and chopped tarragon provide dark green flecks. A light drizzle of extra virgin olive oil catches the light. The setting is a modern bistro with a light oak table. A polished silver spoon and a white cotton napkin lie to the right. Natural window light highlights the creamy texture of the rice.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of chilled dry Vermentino or Pinot Grigio
Offer extra Parmigiano Reggiano at the table
Present in a shallow wide bowl to maintain the fluid consistency
instructions: Heat stock to a simmer in a saucepan.
Cut asparagus tips into 5cm lengths. Dice the remaining stalks into small rounds.
Blanch peas and asparagus tips in boiling water for 2 minutes. Drain and submerge in ice water.
Sauté shallots in olive oil in a wide pan until translucent.
Add rice to the pan. Toast for 2 minutes until edges are translucent.
Pour in wine to deglaze. Stir until the liquid evaporates completely.
Add one ladle of hot stock. Stir constantly until absorbed.
Repeat adding stock gradually. Maintain a gentle simmer.
Add diced asparagus stalks after 10 minutes of cooking.
Continue adding stock until rice is al dente and the texture is fluid.
Remove pan from heat.
Add cold butter and grated cheese. Stir vigorously to create a creamy emulsion.
Fold in blanched peas, asparagus tips, mint, and tarragon.
Stir in lemon juice. Season with salt.
Serve immediately on warmed plates.
notes: The risotto should spread when the plate is tapped from underneath
Keep the stock at a constant simmer to avoid dropping the rice temperature
Use cold butter for the mantecatura to ensure a better emulsion

recipes.recipe_name: Black Rice Tuiles with Red Bean Ganache and Avocado Mousse
recipes.visual_description: Serve on a matte charcoal ceramic platter. Arrange three large, jagged shards of crisp black rice tuile in an overlapping, organic cluster. Pipe five precise 1cm spheres of smooth, dark burgundy red bean ganache and four spheres of vibrant pale green avocado mousse nestled between the rice shards. Place three tiny, purple micro-shiso leaves atop the avocado spheres. Scatter a few grains of Maldon sea salt over the avocado. The composition uses high contrast between the dark rice and bright green mousse. Use a minimalist white marble surface with a single silk-textured grey napkin. Lighting is soft and directional, creating subtle shadows that emphasize the bubbly texture of the fried rice tuiles.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm roasted kukicha or hojicha tea
Present on a traditional raised lacquer tray
Provide small bamboo tongs for communal sharing
instructions: Boil black rice in 400ml water until overcooked and mushy.
Drain rice and blend into a smooth, thick paste.
Spread paste 2mm thick onto a silicone baking mat.
Dehydrate at 60°C for 4 hours until completely brittle.
Break dehydrated rice sheet into large, irregular jagged shards.
Heat oil to 180°C. Flash-fry shards for 5 seconds until puffed. Drain on paper towels.
Simmer red beans in water until tender. Drain well.
Blend warm beans with sugar and butter until a glossy ganache forms.
Pass red bean ganache through a fine-mesh sieve. Cool completely.
Blend avocado flesh with lime juice and honey until light and aerated.
Transfer red bean ganache and avocado mousse into separate piping bags with 1cm plain nozzles.
Pipe alternating spheres of ganache and mousse onto plates. Garnish with rice tuiles.
notes: Ensure the black rice paste is spread evenly to avoid chewy spots after frying.
The avocado mousse must be prepared immediately before serving to prevent oxidation.
The red bean ganache can be made 24 hours in advance if kept refrigerated.

recipes.recipe_name: Pasta al Limone with Pan-Seared Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pasta al Limone served on a clean white porcelain plate. The spaghetti is swirled into a free-flowing mound in the center, glistening with a creamy, pale-yellow lemon-butter emulsion. Large 4cm chunks of golden-brown seared chicken thighs are nestled naturally within and atop the pasta, never sliced or fanned. Fine strands of bright yellow lemon zest and finely chopped green parsley are scattered across the top. The background is a modern bistro setting with a light oak wood table. A white cotton napkin sits to the left of the plate with a polished silver fork. Natural, even daylight illuminates the textures of the seared meat and the silky sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crisp glass of chilled Falanghina or Vermentino wine.
Offer extra finely grated Parmigiano-Reggiano at the table.
Provide crusty ciabatta bread to mop up the lemon-butter sauce.
instructions: Season 4cm chicken chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken until golden and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Boil pasta in salted water until 2 minutes before al dente.
Melt butter in a wide skillet over low heat.
Sauté thinly sliced garlic for 1 minute.
Add lemon zest and juice to the skillet.
Transfer pasta to the skillet with 150ml reserved pasta water.
Increase heat to medium and toss vigorously to emulsify the sauce.
Fold in grated Parmigiano-Reggiano and seared chicken chunks.
Stir until the sauce is glossy and coats the pasta.
Garnish with chopped parsley and serve immediately.
notes: Ensure the pasta water is well-salted like the sea for authentic flavor.
The chicken must reach 75°C to ensure food safety while remaining juicy.
Use high-quality butter for a superior sauce emulsion.

recipes.recipe_name: Chickpea and Cheddar Kofta Curry
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chickpea and Cheddar Kofta Curry served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. Three large, spherical, golden-brown fried koftas are nestled in a velvety, vibrant orange-red tomato and cream sauce. The koftas remain whole, showcasing a crisp, textured exterior. The sauce is finished with a swirl of white cream and bright green cilantro leaves. The bowl sits on a rustic dark wood table next to a piece of charred, bubbly garlic naan. A polished steel spoon rests on a folded grey linen napkin. Natural light from the side emphasizes the contrast between the matte koftas and the glossy, rich gravy, creating an authentic modern Indian bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm garlic naan or steamed basmati rice
Accompany with mango chutney or spicy lime pickle
Provide a side of kachumber salad for fresh acidity
instructions: Mash chickpeas in a large bowl until a coarse paste forms.
Mix in 100g grated cheddar, chickpea flour, and salt until combined.
Shape the mixture into 12 equal spherical balls.
Heat vegetable oil to 180°C in a deep pan.
Fry chickpea balls in batches until deep golden brown. Drain on paper towels.
Heat ghee in a large heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat.
Sauté diced onions until golden brown and caramelized.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in turmeric and chili powder for 30 seconds.
Pour in tomato passata and simmer for 10 minutes until thickened.
Whisk in heavy cream and garam masala. Season with salt.
Place three whole koftas in a shallow bowl and ladle warm sauce over them.
Garnish with remaining cheddar and fresh cilantro.
notes: Do not over-mash the chickpeas; some texture helps the koftas hold their shape.
Ensure the oil is at temperature before frying to prevent the cheese from leaking.
Add the koftas to the sauce immediately before serving to maintain their crispness.

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Chicken Kafta with Tomato-Onion Salad
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of two thick, oval-shaped chicken kafta patties served on a clean white porcelain plate. The chicken is deeply seared to a golden-brown crust, presented as whole pieces stacked slightly to provide height. Beside the meat is a vibrant salad of 1cm diced red tomatoes and finely diced white onions, glistening with olive oil and speckled with dried oregano. The plate features moderate negative space and is set on a light-colored wooden bistro table. Natural morning light highlights the textures of the seared meat and juicy vegetables. A cotton napkin and a polished stainless steel fork and knife are placed neatly beside the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm pita or flatbread
Include a side of garlic-infused yogurt
Provide fresh lemon wedges for acidity
instructions: Combine chicken, garlic, half the onion, cumin, coriander, bread crumbs, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Mix ingredients thoroughly by hand.
Shape mixture into 8 thick, oval-shaped patties.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear patties for 5-6 minutes per side.
Verify internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Mix diced tomatoes with remaining onion and dried oregano.
Toss salad with a drizzle of olive oil and salt.
Place two chicken patties on a plate beside the tomato-onion salad.
notes: Chill the meat mixture for 30 minutes before shaping to prevent sticking.
Ensure the pan is fully hot before adding chicken to achieve a proper crust.
Use fresh ground chicken for the best moisture retention.

recipes.recipe_name: Gnocchi alla Sorrentina
recipes.visual_description: The dish is served in a single-portion shallow white ceramic bowl. The potato gnocchi appear as soft, rounded dumplings thoroughly coated in a rich, velvety San Marzano tomato sauce. Large 2cm chunks of buffalo mozzarella are distributed throughout, some melted into the sauce and others forming a bubbly, golden-brown crust on the surface. Fresh, vibrant green basil leaves are placed as a final garnish, providing a color contrast against the deep red sauce. The presentation is rustic yet refined, with visible olive oil droplets on the surface. The bowl sits on a dark oak table with a white cotton napkin and a polished silver fork to the side.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Pane di Altamura for scarpetta
Pair with a chilled Gragnano or Aglianico wine
Present in individual terracotta 'pignatiello' dishes
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Sauté crushed garlic cloves until golden. Remove and discard garlic.
Add hand-crushed San Marzano tomatoes and salt to the pan.
Simmer sauce for 20 minutes until thick and glossy.
Boil gnocchi in salted water until they float to the surface.
Drain gnocchi and transfer directly into the tomato sauce.
Tear half the basil leaves and stir into the pasta.
Fold in half of the mozzarella cut into 2cm chunks and the grated Pecorino.
Divide the mixture into four individual ceramic baking dishes.
Top with remaining mozzarella chunks.
Broil for 5 minutes until cheese is bubbling and develops golden spots.
Garnish with remaining fresh basil leaves.
notes: Ensure mozzarella is well-drained to prevent a watery sauce
Do not overcook gnocchi in water as they continue cooking in the oven
Use only high-quality DOP San Marzano tomatoes for authentic flavor

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Beef and Potato Tapas
recipes.visual_description: A rustic Spanish tapas presentation on a clean white porcelain plate. The base features golden, roasted potato cubes with crisp edges. Thick, seared beef chunks are nestled among the potatoes, showing a deep brown crust. Vibrant green beans, blanched and sautéed, are tucked between the beef and potatoes, adding a fresh vertical element. Sliced golden garlic chips and a light dusting of smoked paprika provide textural contrast and color. The dish is finished with a glossy drizzle of extra virgin olive oil. The setting is a modern bistro with a light oak table, a simple linen napkin, and even natural lighting that highlights the textures of the seared meat and roasted vegetables.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in traditional clay cazuelas
Accompany with crusty bread
Provide small wooden skewers for sharing
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Peel and cut potatoes into 2cm cubes.
Toss potatoes with 20ml olive oil and salt.
Roast potatoes on a baking tray for 25 minutes until golden.
Trim ends of green beans.
Boil beans in salted water for 3 minutes.
Transfer beans to ice water to stop cooking. Drain well.
Cut beef into 3cm chunks.
Season beef with salt and pepper.
Heat 20ml olive oil in a heavy skillet over high heat.
Sear beef chunks for 2 minutes per side for medium-rare.
Remove beef from pan and let rest for 5 minutes.
Heat remaining 40ml olive oil in the same pan over medium heat.
Fry garlic slices until light golden and crisp.
Add green beans and smoked paprika to the garlic oil.
Toss for 1 minute to coat and warm through.
Combine beef, potatoes, and beans on a serving platter.
notes: Ensure potatoes are completely dry before roasting for maximum crispness.
Do not crowd the pan when searing beef to maintain a high temperature.
Use high-quality Spanish smoked paprika for authentic flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Prosciutto-Wrapped Chicken with Balsamic Radicchio
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of prosciutto-wrapped chicken served on a large, clean white porcelain plate. The hero is a whole, golden-brown seared chicken breast wrapped in crispy prosciutto, positioned slightly off-center. Beneath it lies a bed of vibrant green arugula and two wedges of pan-sautéed radicchio, showing charred edges and a glossy balsamic glaze. Pitted black olives are scattered naturally around the base. The dish is finished with wide, thin shavings of Pecorino Romano cheese and a small sprig of fresh rosemary. The lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the textures of the crispy meat and wilted greens. The background is a dark wood bistro table with a folded grey cotton napkin and a simple fork.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty ciabatta bread
Pair with a medium-bodied Italian red wine like Chianti Classico
instructions: Season chicken breasts with black pepper.
Wrap each breast tightly with two slices of prosciutto.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken for 6 minutes per side until the internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from the pan and let rest whole.
Cut the radicchio into eight wedges.
Add remaining oil and radicchio wedges to the skillet.
Sauté radicchio for 3 minutes until edges are charred.
Add rosemary sprigs and halved black olives to the pan.
Pour in balsamic vinegar to deglaze the skillet.
Simmer for 2 minutes until the vinegar thickens into a glaze.
Arrange a bed of arugula on four plates.
Place two radicchio wedges and olives over the arugula.
Position one whole chicken breast on top of the vegetables.
Shave Pecorino Romano into thin curls over the dish.
notes: Do not add extra salt to the chicken as the prosciutto and Romano cheese provide sufficient salinity.
Ensure the skillet is hot before adding the chicken to achieve a crispy prosciutto exterior.

recipes.recipe_name: Loganberry and Pina Colada Red Curry with Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Thai red curry served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The curry sauce is a rich, creamy orange-red with a slight oil sheen on the surface. Thick chunks of seared chicken thigh are piled in the center, surrounded by whole, dark purple loganberries. Bright green Thai basil leaves and fine julienne strips of fresh red chili are scattered across the top for contrast. The bowl is placed on a light teak wood table. Beside it sits a small, matching bowl of fluffy, steamed jasmine rice. Traditional Thai stainless steel spoon and fork rest on a folded white cotton napkin. Natural light illuminates the textures of the glossy sauce and tender meat.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice in a separate bowl
Use a traditional Thai spoon and fork for dining
Include a side of Prik Nam Pla (fish sauce with chilies)
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Fry red curry paste for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add chicken chunks and sear for 4 minutes until browned.
Pour in coconut milk and pina colada mix.
Add torn kaffir lime leaves and simmer for 10 minutes.
Check chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Stir in elderflower syrup, fish sauce, palm sugar, and citric acid.
Add loganberries and simmer for 1 minute to warm through.
Fold in Thai basil leaves and remove from heat.
Serve immediately with steamed jasmine rice.
notes: The citric acid balances the sweetness of the pina colada mix.
Do not overcook the loganberries to maintain their structure.
The elderflower provides a floral note similar to traditional jasmine water.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo con Crema de Rábano y Pepinillos
recipes.visual_description: A single whole seared chicken breast sits centered on a traditional matte-finish clay plate. The chicken features a deep golden-brown crust and is generously coated in a velvety, ivory-colored horseradish cream sauce. Small, uniform 5mm cubes of bright green pickled cucumbers are scattered over the top, offering a sharp textural contrast. Freshly chopped cilantro leaves provide vibrant green accents. The sauce pools naturally around the base of the meat, exhibiting a thick, glossy consistency. The background features a rustic wooden table with a small basket of warm corn tortillas tucked into a white cotton cloth, creating an authentic Mexican bistro atmosphere under soft, natural lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Accompany with a side of Mexican red rice
Provide extra lime wedges for acidity
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry with paper towels.
Season chicken on both sides with salt, pepper, and ground cumin.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken in the skillet. Sear for 6 minutes per side.
Verify internal temperature reaches 75°C using a meat thermometer.
Remove chicken from the pan and let rest on a warm plate.
In the same skillet, sauté onion and garlic for 3 minutes until translucent.
Add grated horseradish and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in chicken stock to deglaze the pan. Scrape up browned bits.
Simmer liquid until reduced by half.
Reduce heat to low. Whisk in Mexican crema until smooth and thickened.
Place chicken back into the sauce for 1 minute to coat.
Garnish with diced pickled cucumbers and fresh cilantro before serving.
notes: Use fresh horseradish for the best heat profile.
Ensure the pan is hot before adding chicken to achieve a proper sear.
Do not boil the sauce after adding crema to prevent curdling.

recipes.recipe_name: Asparagus and Pea Risotto with Fresh Herbs
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of vibrant green risotto served on a wide, flat white porcelain rimmed plate. The risotto has a fluid 'all'onda' consistency, spreading naturally across the plate without a ring mold. Bright green blanched asparagus tips, cut into 5cm lengths, are placed organically on top. Whole blanched peas are scattered throughout the rice. Fine ribbons of fresh mint and chopped tarragon provide dark green flecks. A light drizzle of extra virgin olive oil catches the light. The setting is a modern bistro with a light oak table. A polished silver spoon and a white cotton napkin lie to the right. Natural window light highlights the creamy texture of the rice.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of chilled dry Vermentino or Pinot Grigio
Offer extra Parmigiano Reggiano at the table
Present in a shallow wide bowl to maintain the fluid consistency
instructions: Heat stock to a simmer in a saucepan.
Cut asparagus tips into 5cm lengths. Dice the remaining stalks into small rounds.
Blanch peas and asparagus tips in boiling water for 2 minutes. Drain and submerge in ice water.
Sauté shallots in olive oil in a wide pan until translucent.
Add rice to the pan. Toast for 2 minutes until edges are translucent.
Pour in wine to deglaze. Stir until the liquid evaporates completely.
Add one ladle of hot stock. Stir constantly until absorbed.
Repeat adding stock gradually. Maintain a gentle simmer.
Add diced asparagus stalks after 10 minutes of cooking.
Continue adding stock until rice is al dente and the texture is fluid.
Remove pan from heat.
Add cold butter and grated cheese. Stir vigorously to create a creamy emulsion.
Fold in blanched peas, asparagus tips, mint, and tarragon.
Stir in lemon juice. Season with salt.
Serve immediately on warmed plates.
notes: The risotto should spread when the plate is tapped from underneath
Keep the stock at a constant simmer to avoid dropping the rice temperature
Use cold butter for the mantecatura to ensure a better emulsion

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken Thighs with Thyme and Avocado Crema
recipes.visual_description: A single portion presented on a clean, wide white porcelain plate. Two whole roasted chicken thighs sit at the center, featuring deeply browned, crispy skin flecked with charred thyme leaves. To the side, a vibrant, pale green avocado crema is spread in a smooth, professional swoop. The crema has a glossy, velvety texture. Small drops of golden olive oil are drizzled over the crema. A few fresh, bright green thyme sprigs are placed as a final garnish. The plate sits on a light oak wood table in a bright bistro setting. Natural light emphasizes the contrast between the rustic, textured chicken skin and the refined, matte finish of the avocado puree. A folded white linen napkin and silver fork are placed neatly to the right.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough bread
Pair with a crisp dry white wine
Present on pre-warmed ceramic plates
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels.
Mix 30ml olive oil, half the thyme, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Rub oil mixture thoroughly over chicken skin and underside.
Place chicken on a baking tray.
Roast for 25-30 minutes until skin is crispy.
Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Scoop avocado flesh into a blender.
Add yogurt, lemon juice, garlic, and remaining olive oil.
Blend until completely smooth and thick.
Spread a thick layer of avocado crema on each plate.
Place two whole roasted chicken thighs on the crema.
Garnish with remaining fresh thyme sprigs.
notes: Ensure avocados are fully ripe for a smooth crema texture
Rest the chicken for 5 minutes before plating to retain juices
Use high-quality extra virgin olive oil for the finishing drizzle

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken Thighs with Pepperoncini
recipes.visual_description: Two whole roasted chicken thighs served on a clean white porcelain plate. The chicken skin is golden-brown and crispy with visible lemon pepper specks. Thighs are presented whole, not sliced. Surrounding the chicken are roasted baby potato halves and large chunks of charred red bell pepper. Sliced yellow-green pepperoncini rings are scattered over the dish. One whole pepperoncini is placed as a garnish. A light, savory glaze from the Italian dressing coats the ingredients. The plate is set on a dark wood bistro table. A white cotton napkin and polished flatware sit beside the plate. Natural, even lighting emphasizes the glistening textures and vibrant colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm, crusty Italian bread to soak up juices
Accompany with a simple arugula salad
Present in the roasting pan for family-style dining
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken dry with paper towels.
Season chicken with lemon pepper and oregano.
Place chicken, potatoes, and peppers in a roasting pan.
Toss vegetables with olive oil and smashed garlic.
Pour Italian dressing over chicken and vegetables.
Scatter sliced pepperoncini throughout the pan.
Roast for 40 minutes until chicken skin is golden.
Confirm chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Rest chicken 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use a high-quality oil-based Italian dressing for the best crust
Ensure the roasting pan is large enough to prevent steaming
The acidity of the pepperoncini balances the richness of the chicken skin

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Biryani
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken Biryani served on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish features a mound of long-grain Basmati rice. The rice displays a natural color variation from pale white to deep orange-yellow from the spice infusion. Two large, bone-in chicken thigh chunks are nestled within the rice. The chicken is tender and coated in a thick, savory masala. Topping the rice are thin, golden-brown fried onion strips and vibrant green sprigs of fresh coriander. The arrangement is organic and centered with moderate negative space. A small ceramic bowl of white yogurt raita sits to the side. The background is a dark wood bistro table with a folded linen napkin and a polished brass spoon.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of cucumber raita
Accompany with lime wedges and sliced raw red onions
Traditional brass or copper serving spoon

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs, bone-in, cut into large chunks

instructions: Wash rice until water runs clear. Soak in water for 30 minutes.
Mix chicken chunks with yogurt, spice mix, ginger-garlic paste, and 5g salt. Marinate for 1 hour.
Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pot. Fry sliced onions until dark golden brown. Remove half for garnish.
Boil 1.5 L water with 10g salt. Add soaked rice. Cook until 70% tender. Drain immediately.
Add marinated chicken to the pot with remaining onions and ghee. Cook for 5 minutes over medium heat.
Layer the parboiled rice over the chicken chunks. Top with reserved fried onions, coriander, and mint.
Cover pot with a tight-fitting lid. Use a heavy weight or dough to seal steam inside.
Cook on very low heat for 25 minutes. Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Turn off heat. Let the pot rest for 10 minutes before opening.
Gently fluff the rice from the sides to mix colors without breaking grains.
notes: Do not overcook the rice during the initial boil or it will turn mushy during the steaming phase.
Use a heavy-bottomed pot (like a Dutch oven) to prevent the bottom layer of chicken from burning.

recipes.recipe_name: Authentic Aloo Murgh Curry
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a vibrant, thick tomato-based gravy with a deep reddish-orange hue. Large 4cm chunks of tender, simmered chicken and 3cm cubes of softened yellow potatoes are the focal points. Bright 2cm squares of sautéed red pepper provide color contrast. The curry is presented in a traditional hammered copper karahi bowl placed on a clean wooden table. A generous garnish of coarsely chopped fresh green coriander sits on top. To the side, a small mound of fluffy white basmati rice and a folded piece of charred naan bread are visible. The lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the glossy texture of the sauce and the rustic surface of the table.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm garlic naan
Accompany with steamed basmati rice
Side of cucumber raita
Fresh lime wedges on the side
instructions: Combine chicken chunks with yogurt, lemon juice, half the garlic, and 1 tablespoon curry powder.
Marinate chicken for 30 minutes in the refrigerator.
Heat oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Sauté diced red onions until dark golden brown.
Add remaining garlic and remaining curry powder. Stir for 1 minute.
Mix in tomato puree and salt. Cook until oil separates from the sauce.
Add marinated chicken chunks. Brown the meat for 5 minutes.
Incorporate potato cubes and red pepper squares.
Pour in 300ml water. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook for 25 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Confirm chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Garnish with fresh coriander.
notes: Use waxy potatoes to ensure they hold their shape during simmering.
For extra heat, add fresh green chilies with the garlic.
Ensure onions are properly browned to develop the base umami of the gravy.

recipes.recipe_name: Salt-Crusted Sea Bass with Roasted Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A whole sea bass fillet, moist and glistening, sits centered on a clean white porcelain plate. The skin is removed to reveal ivory-colored flakes. Beside it, four roasted baby potato halves show deep golden-brown caramelized edges and tender centers. A small pile of cracked, snowy-white salt crust remains on the side as a rustic visual element. A vibrant green sprig of fresh parsley and a charred lemon half provide color contrast. The lighting is natural and bright, highlighting the texture of the fish. The background is a light oak bistro table with a folded white cotton napkin and a simple silver fork. The composition is balanced with clean negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Drizzle with high-quality extra virgin olive oil at the table
Serve with a crisp, dry Mediterranean white wine
Present the intact salt crust to guests before cracking and filleting
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss baby potatoes with olive oil, garlic, and salt on a baking tray.
Roast potatoes for 30 minutes until golden.
Mix coarse salt with egg whites in a large bowl until it feels like damp sand.
Stuff fish cavities with lemon slices, rosemary, and thyme.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Spread a 1cm layer of salt mixture on the parchment.
Place fish on the salt bed.
Cover fish completely with remaining salt, pressing firmly to seal.
Bake fish for 25 minutes.
Rest fish for 5 minutes before cracking the crust.
Carefully remove salt pieces and fish skin.
Serve fillets immediately.
notes: Keep scales on the fish to protect the flesh from absorbing too much salt
Ensure the salt crust has no gaps to trap steam effectively

recipes.recipe_name: Sicilian Watermelon Pudding
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Sicilian Watermelon Pudding served in a clear glass bowl on a rustic wooden table. The pudding is a vibrant, translucent ruby red, set into a soft, spoonable gel. Small dark chocolate chips are visible throughout the pudding, mimicking watermelon seeds. The top is lightly dusted with a pinch of ground cinnamon and a generous sprinkle of bright green, roughly chopped pistachios. The bowl sits on a simple white ceramic saucer. A small silver dessert spoon rests beside the bowl on a linen napkin. The lighting is warm and natural, suggesting a late afternoon in a Mediterranean kitchen. The entire plate and immediate table setting are visible.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve cold as a summer palate cleanser
Accompany with a glass of Passito di Pantelleria wine
Traditionally served in small glass cups
instructions: Blend watermelon flesh until smooth.
Strain juice through a fine sieve to collect 1 liter.
Whisk cornstarch and sugar into cold juice in a large pot.
Cook over medium heat while stirring constantly.
Remove from heat once mixture thickens and turns translucent.
Stir in ground cinnamon.
Let cool to room temperature.
Fold in chocolate chips.
Pour mixture into four individual serving bowls.
Chill in refrigerator for 4 hours until firm.
Top with crushed pistachios.
notes: Use a very ripe watermelon for best color
Adjust sugar based on fruit sweetness
Ensure the mixture is fully translucent before removing from heat

recipes.recipe_name: Tajin-Rubbed Chicken with Tomatillo Salsa and Oaxaca Cheese
recipes.visual_description: A single portion featuring two whole, bone-in chicken thighs served on a clean white porcelain plate. The chicken skin is a deep golden-red from the Tajin crust. Melted white Oaxaca cheese blankets the top of the chicken, showing a soft, stringy texture. The chicken sits atop a vibrant, textured green tomatillo salsa spread across the center of the plate. A few fresh cilantro leaves are scattered over the top. The arrangement is clean with moderate negative space. The background is a dark wood bistro table. A small side dish of warm, folded corn tortillas rests nearby. Natural, even lighting highlights the contrast between the red spice, white cheese, and green sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas kept in a cloth-lined basket
Accompany with a side of Mexican red rice or black beans
Offer extra lime wedges on the side for acidity
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Place tomatillos, onion, garlic, and serrano pepper on a baking sheet.
Roast vegetables for 15 minutes until charred and softened.
Transfer roasted vegetables and any juices to a blender.
Add cilantro and lime juice. Pulse until slightly chunky. Season with salt.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels.
Rub Tajin seasoning evenly over the skin and underside of the chicken.
Heat oil in a large oven-proof skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden and crisp.
Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to the oven.
Roast chicken until the internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Top each chicken thigh with Oaxaca cheese.
Return to oven for 2 minutes until cheese is melted and bubbling.
Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.
Spread tomatillo salsa on plates. Place chicken thighs on top.
notes: Ensure tomatillos are rinsed thoroughly to remove the sticky residue.
Oaxaca cheese can be substituted with Monterey Jack or Mozzarella if unavailable.
Do not crowd the pan when searing to ensure the skin becomes crispy.

recipes.recipe_name: Oyster Ice Cream with Sea Salt Caramel and Nori Tuile
recipes.visual_description: A single, pristine ivory-colored sphere of oyster-infused ice cream sits off-center in a shallow, matte-black designer ceramic bowl. The ice cream has a smooth, velvet-like texture. Next to it rests one whole, translucent oyster poached in vanilla-infused syrup, glistening with a high-gloss sheen. A thin, dark green, rectangular nori tuile provides architectural height, leaning against the ice cream. Precise droplets of deep amber sea salt caramel are positioned around the base. The arrangement uses significant negative space on a grey-veined white marble surface. Lighting is directional, creating sharp, clean shadows. A polished silver dessert spoon rests on a folded white linen napkin nearby.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a chilled glass of Sauternes or late-harvest Riesling
Use a small, chilled silver dessert spoon
instructions: Shuck oysters. Reserve 20ml of the filtered brine.
Roughly chop 4 oysters. Combine with milk and cream in a saucepan.
Heat to 80°C. Remove from heat. Steep for 20 minutes.
Blend the mixture. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve.
Whisk egg yolks with 80g sugar until pale.
Temper the oyster cream into the yolks. Cook to 82°C while stirring.
Chill the custard over an ice bath. Stir in the reserved brine. Churn in an ice cream maker.
Prepare a simple syrup with 50g sugar and 50ml water. Simmer the remaining 2 whole oysters for 2 minutes. Chill.
Melt 20g sugar until dark amber. Whisk in 20ml warm cream and sea salt to make caramel.
Blend nori, melted butter, flour, and egg whites into a paste.
Spread thinly on a silicone mat. Bake at 170°C for 5 minutes. Shape while warm.
Place a sphere of ice cream in a chilled bowl. Top with one whole poached oyster. Drizzle caramel and garnish with a nori tuile shard.
notes: Ensure oysters are extremely fresh for the best flavor profile.
The brine adds necessary salinity to balance the sugar.
Do not boil the custard or the oyster flavor will turn metallic.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Stuffed Zucchini with Olive and Cheese Crust
recipes.visual_description: Two whole roasted zucchini halves rest centrally on a large, round white porcelain plate. A bubbly, golden-brown crust of toasted bread crumbs and melted cheese covers the top. Vibrant green zucchini skins contrast with the dark filling of wilted spinach and chopped black olives. Beside the zucchini, a neat mound of diced red tomatoes and 2cm avocado cubes provides fresh color. A light drizzle of creamy mustard-mayonnaise sauce accents the plate in an organic, flowing pattern. Placed on a light oak table with a folded white cotton napkin, the scene uses natural light to highlight textures of the crunchy topping and succulent vegetables. The composition is balanced with professional negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough bread
Pair with a chilled dry white wine
Present as a light lunch or a sophisticated dinner centerpiece
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Halve zucchinis lengthwise. Scoop out centers to create 1cm thick shells.
Finely dice the scooped zucchini flesh, red onion, and garlic.
Sauté onion and garlic in a pan with oil for 3 minutes.
Add diced zucchini flesh and spinach. Cook until spinach wilts and moisture evaporates.
Remove from heat. Stir in chopped olives and 75g of cheese.
Fill zucchini shells with the mixture.
Combine bread crumbs, remaining 75g cheese, and cayenne pepper in a bowl.
Press the crumb mixture firmly onto the zucchini filling.
Bake for 20 minutes until the crust is golden and zucchinis are tender.
Whisk mayonnaise and mustard together until smooth.
Dice tomatoes and avocado into 2cm cubes.
Place two zucchini halves on each plate.
Serve with a side of tomato and avocado cubes.
Drizzle the mustard-mayonnaise sauce over the dish.
notes: Ensure spinach is squeezed dry after sautéing to prevent a soggy filling.
Use a sharp spoon to scoop zucchini centers without piercing the skin.
Adjust cayenne pepper for desired heat level.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Mango and Cultured Almond Parfait
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of the dessert is presented in a handcrafted, matte-finished cream ceramic bowl. The base consists of a thick, velvety layer of ivory-colored cultured almond cream. Resting on the cream are 1cm cubes of vibrant, glistening orange lacto-fermented mango, arranged in a loose, organic cluster. A textured soil made from toasted, golden-brown cookie crumbs and almond pulp is scattered across one side, providing a rustic contrast. A thin, amber-colored syrup made from upcycled mango skins is drizzled over the fruit. The plate is set on a reclaimed light oak table with a natural beige linen napkin. The lighting is soft and natural, emphasizing the creamy and crunchy textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small carved wooden spoon
Present on a stone or reclaimed wood coaster
Pair with a tea made from dried mango scraps
instructions: Peel mangoes. Reserve skins and pits.
Dice mango flesh into 1cm cubes.
Combine mango cubes, salt, and honey in a sterile jar.
Ferment at room temperature for 48 hours. Refrigerate.
Simmer mango skins and pits in 100ml water for 10 minutes.
Strain and reduce liquid to a thick syrup. Cool.
Blend soaked almonds with 150ml water until smooth.
Strain through a fine cloth. Reserve the almond pulp.
Stir probiotic powder into the almond milk.
Culture at 30°C for 12 hours until thick.
Crumble cookies and mix with the reserved almond pulp.
Toast mixture at 150°C for 15 minutes until golden.
Place cultured almond cream into four bowls.
Add fermented mango cubes in a cluster.
Scatter cookie soil over the cream and drizzle with mango syrup.
notes: Use organic mangoes to ensure skins are safe for syrup
Adjust fermentation time based on kitchen temperature
Cookie soil can be stored in an airtight container for 5 days

recipes.recipe_name: Ayam Goreng Sambal
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Ayam Goreng Sambal is presented on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish consists of two whole, bone-in chicken thighs, deep-fried to a dark golden-brown. Each piece is heavily coated in a thick, textured red sambal sauce containing visible chili seeds and minced shallots. Two bright green kaffir lime leaves and a stalk of lemongrass are placed as garnishes. The chicken is arranged in a natural cluster, avoiding any slicing or fanning. The background features a dark wooden table with a side bowl of white jasmine rice and a simple cotton napkin. Natural light emphasizes the glossy, oily sheen of the chili paste.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm jasmine rice
Accompany with fresh cucumber slices and cabbage
Pair with fried tempeh and tofu
instructions: Rub chicken thighs with salt and turmeric powder.
Heat coconut oil in a deep pan to 175°C.
Fry chicken thighs until golden brown.
Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken and drain on paper towels.
Reserve 30 ml of frying oil in a clean sauté pan.
Sauté shallots, garlic, galangal, and lemongrass until fragrant.
Add sambal ulek and kaffir lime leaves to the pan.
Stir in palm sugar until dissolved.
Toss the fried chicken thighs in the sambal mixture to coat thoroughly.
Serve immediately while hot.
notes: Sauté the sambal until the oil separates for authentic depth of flavor.
Use fresh kaffir lime leaves for the most aromatic result.

recipes.recipe_name: Chocolate Graham Cracker Layer Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single square portion of the layer cake sits centered on a white ceramic plate. The side view reveals distinct, horizontal layers: softened tan graham cracker sheets alternating with thick, ivory cream cheese filling and dark chocolate pudding. The top is coated in a uniform, matte layer of fine dark cocoa powder. The crackers are cut into clean, sharp-edged squares. A stainless steel dessert spoon rests on a white paper towel beside the plate. The scene is set on a well-used dark oak kitchen table under warm, soft overhead lighting. Small, natural graham cracker crumbs accent the base of the cake. The entire plate is visible, showing a balance of textures and natural colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve chilled directly from the refrigerator.
Pair with a glass of cold milk or a hot cup of black coffee.
instructions: Whisk chocolate pudding mix and cold milk in a bowl for 2 minutes.
Beat cream cheese, powdered sugar, and vanilla in a separate bowl until smooth.
Fold half of the prepared chocolate pudding into the cream cheese mixture.
Place a single layer of whole graham crackers in the bottom of a square container.
Spread half of the cream cheese mixture evenly over the crackers.
Add a second layer of graham crackers on top.
Spread the remaining chocolate pudding over the second cracker layer.
Add a third layer of graham crackers.
Top with the remaining cream cheese mixture and smooth the surface.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours to soften the crackers.
Dust the top heavily with cocoa powder through a fine sieve before slicing.
Cut into 4 large square portions to serve.
notes: Ensure the cream cheese is fully at room temperature to avoid lumps.
For cleaner slices, wipe the knife blade between every cut.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato and Tomato Salad with Hollandaise Dressing
recipes.visual_description: A large ceramic platter holds the salad on a well-worn wooden kitchen table. The base features a bed of roughly chopped, vibrant green romaine lettuce. On top, 1cm thick rounds of boiled potatoes are layered casually with bright red, thinly sliced tomato wedges. Delicate, translucent red onion rings are scattered across the vegetables. A creamy, pale yellow hollandaise sauce is drizzled in organic patterns, partially coating the potato rounds. The arrangement is natural and unpretentious, with ingredients overlapping. The scene is captured in warm, soft kitchen light, showing the entire plate. A simple linen napkin and a stainless steel fork rest beside the platter, creating a lived-in, authentic home dining atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm as a light lunch
Accompany with crusty baguette slices
instructions: Boil potatoes in salted water until tender.
Drain potatoes and let cool for 10 minutes.
