Beside the bowl sits a small side of steamed bok choy halves, vibrant green and crisp-tender. A pair of dark wood chopsticks rests on a ceramic holder. The background is a clean, dark wood table with a simple linen napkin. The entire plate is visible, showing the rich contrast between the dark, caramelized pork and the white vessel.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice
Accompany with blanched bok choy
Provide dark wood chopsticks and a ceramic rice bowl
instructions: Place pork cubes in a pot of cold water. Bring to a boil.
Blanch for 5 minutes. Drain and rinse with warm water.
Heat oil and rock sugar in a wok over low heat.
Stir until sugar melts and turns deep amber.
Add pork cubes. Stir to coat thoroughly in caramel.
Add Shaoxing wine, light soy sauce, and dark soy sauce.
Add ginger, green onion knots, star anise, and cinnamon.
Pour in boiling water to cover the meat.
Simmer covered on low heat for 60 minutes until tender.
Remove lid. Increase heat to high.
Stir constantly until the liquid reduces to a thick, glossy glaze.
notes: Use rock sugar instead of granulated sugar for a glossier finish.
Always use boiling water for braising to keep the meat tender.
Do not skip the blanching step to ensure a clean flavor profile.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Rocoto and Carob Braised Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A wide white porcelain bowl contains a rich, mahogany-colored braise. Large, thick chunks of seared Portobello mushrooms serve as the focal point, coated in a glossy, deep purple-brown sauce. The sauce exhibits a velvety sheen from the almond butter and oat milk. Bright red specks of finely diced rocoto pepper provide sharp color contrast against the dark reduction. A neat mound of fluffy white quinoa sits to the side, providing a clean neutral base. Fresh cilantro leaves are scattered naturally across the top. The dish is presented on a light wood table with a folded cotton napkin and a traditional Peruvian woven textile accent in the background. Natural light highlights the moist, meaty texture of the mushroom chunks.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of fluffy white quinoa or boiled yellow potatoes.
Accompany with Salsa Criolla (pickled red onions and lime).
Serve in a deep ceramic bowl to retain heat.

ingredients.name: Portobello mushrooms, cut into thick chunks
Rocoto peppers, seeded and finely diced

instructions: Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Sauté onion and garlic for 5 minutes until soft.
Add diced rocoto peppers. Cook for 3 minutes.
Add mushroom chunks. Sear for 6 minutes until browned.
Whisk almond butter, carob, acai, and coconut sugar into the oat milk.
Pour vegetable stock into the pot. Stir in the milk mixture.
Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes until the sauce reduces and thickens.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot with quinoa or rice.
notes: Rocoto peppers are quite spicy; adjust quantity to control heat levels.
Carob and acai provide an earthy depth similar to a Mexican mole.
Ensure the sauce reaches a nappe consistency to coat the mushrooms properly.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef Roulades with Ham and Cheese in Tomato Cream Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of two whole, golden-brown beef roulades rests on a clean white porcelain plate. The rolls are unsliced, showing a seared, textured exterior. They are nestled in a smooth, vibrant orange-pink sauce made from simmered tomatoes, milk, and yogurt. The sauce has a glossy, fluid consistency and pools naturally around the meat. Small specks of dried oregano are visible in the sauce. A garnish of fresh, bright green flat-leaf parsley is placed on top. The plate is set on a light oak wooden table in a sunlit bistro. A folded white cotton napkin and polished stainless steel cutlery sit beside the plate, creating a professional yet approachable presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with buttery mashed potatoes or boiled egg noodles
Pair with a glass of medium-bodied red wine
Accompany with a side of crusty sourdough bread to soak up the sauce
instructions: Flatten beef steaks to 5mm thickness using a meat mallet.
Season both sides of the beef with salt and pepper.
Place one slice of ham and 25g of cheese on each steak.
Roll the beef tightly around the filling and secure with toothpicks.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear the roulades for 2 minutes per side until deeply browned.
Remove the meat from the skillet and set aside.
Add diced onion to the same skillet and sauté for 3 minutes.
Stir in garlic and oregano and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and milk, stirring to combine.
Place the beef rolls back into the sauce.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 25 minutes.
Remove from heat and gently whisk in the yogurt until the sauce is smooth.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve immediately.
notes: Ensure the yogurt is at room temperature before adding to prevent curdling
Do not boil the sauce once the yogurt has been added
Remove toothpicks before serving to guests

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Steel-Cut Oat Risotto with Spiced Cashews and Fruit
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a shallow white porcelain bowl. The oat risotto has a creamy, fluid consistency, spreading naturally across the base. It is a soft golden color from the turmeric. In the center, a clean dollop of thick white Greek yogurt provides contrast. Whole toasted cashews are scattered around the yogurt, showing deep golden-brown roasted spots. Bright red pomegranate seeds are sprinkled across the surface, adding vibrant pops of color. The chia seeds appear as tiny dark flecks throughout the oats. A few fresh cilantro leaves are placed off-center. The setting is a rustic wooden table with a linen napkin and a silver spoon. Lighting is soft and natural.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in wide, shallow bowls
Accompany with warm flatbread
Pair with a chilled savory lassi
instructions: Toast cashews in a dry pan over medium heat until golden. Set aside.
Melt butter in a heavy-bottomed pot.
Add cumin seeds and toast until fragrant.
Add diced onion and garlic. Sauté for 5 minutes until translucent.
Stir in oats and turmeric. Toast for 2 minutes.
Pour in 200ml whey. Stir continuously until liquid is absorbed.
Add remaining whey in 200ml increments. Stir frequently until oats are tender but retain texture.
Stir in chia seeds 5 minutes before cooking is complete.
Remove pot from heat. Fold in 150g of yogurt to achieve a fluid consistency.
Season with salt and pepper.
Divide risotto into four shallow bowls.
Top each portion with a dollop of remaining yogurt, toasted cashews, and pomegranate seeds.
Garnish with cilantro leaves.
notes: Ensure the whey is at room temperature before adding to the oats
Do not overcook the oats; they should have a slight bite similar to al dente rice
Adjust the amount of whey for a looser, more fluid texture

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Garlic Chicken with Pan con Tomate and Charred Corn
recipes.visual_description: The dish features two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with crisp, mahogany-colored skin. They sit atop a bed of vibrant yellow corn kernels, charred to show dark brown spots. Several whole, golden-brown garlic cloves are scattered naturally around the chicken. Beside the meat, a thick slice of toasted rustic sourdough bread is generously topped with a bright red, textured tomato pulp and a glistening drizzle of extra virgin olive oil. The plate is clean white porcelain, providing a sharp contrast to the warm tones of the food. Finely chopped green parsley is sprinkled over the chicken for color. The setting is a dark wood bistro table with natural, soft lighting and a simple linen napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Spanish Manzanilla olives
Pair with a glass of chilled white wine from Rueda
Present on traditional hand-painted Spanish ceramics
instructions: Season chicken with salt, pepper, and smoked paprika.
Heat 40 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down in the pan.
Sear for 8 minutes until skin is crisp and golden.
Turn chicken over. Add whole garlic cloves to the pan.
Reduce heat to medium. Cook until chicken reaches 75°C internally.
Remove chicken and garlic. Rest for 5 minutes.
Add corn kernels to the same skillet. Char for 4 minutes until blackened in spots.
Grate tomatoes into a bowl. Mix with 20 ml olive oil and salt.
Toast bread slices until golden. Rub with one raw garlic clove.
Spread tomato mixture over the toasted bread.
Plate two chicken thighs with charred corn and garlic. Serve with the bread.
notes: Use very ripe tomatoes for the best pan con tomate results
Keep the garlic cloves whole to prevent burning and achieve a sweet, confit texture
Ensure the skillet is very hot before adding corn to achieve a proper char without overcooking

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Mango Chicken Curry
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a vibrant green curry served in a traditional shallow ceramic bowl. Large 3cm succulent chicken chunks are the focal point, glistening with a creamy coconut-based sauce. Interspersed among the chicken are bright yellow 2cm mango cubes, providing a sharp color contrast against the pale green liquid. Torn dark green Thai basil leaves and thin diagonal slices of red chili garnish the top. Beside the bowl sits a perfectly formed mound of fluffy, white jasmine rice. The plating is clean with moderate negative space on a dark wood table. A simple white porcelain plate holds the bowl. A traditional Thai brass spoon and fork lie on a folded cotton napkin. Natural light highlights the silky texture of the curry.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Prik Nam Pla (fish sauce with sliced chilies)
Eat using a spoon in the right hand and a fork in the left to push food onto the spoon
Pair with a cold Thai iced tea
instructions: Rinse jasmine rice until water runs clear. Cook in 600ml water until fluffy.
Cut chicken thighs into 3cm chunks.
Spoon 100ml of the thickest coconut cream into a wok over medium heat.
Boil cream until it separates and oil appears on the surface.
Add curry paste to the oil. Fry for 2 minutes until aromatic.
Add chicken chunks. Sear for 3 minutes until exterior is opaque.
Pour in remaining coconut milk and chicken stock. Add torn lime leaves.
Simmer for 10 minutes. Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar. Adjust for savory-sweet balance.
Fold in mango cubes and Thai basil. Remove from heat immediately.
Serve curry in a bowl next to the jasmine rice.
notes: Use high-fat canned coconut milk to ensure the cream 'cracks' properly during tempering
Add mango at the very end to prevent it from dissolving into the sauce
Ensure the chicken chunks are uniform in size for even cooking

recipes.recipe_name: Japanese Braised Pork Belly (Buta no Kakuni)
recipes.visual_description: Three large, 5cm cubes of braised pork belly are centered in a shallow, matte white ceramic bowl. The pork has a deep mahogany glaze and visible layers of tender meat and fat. One soft-boiled egg, sliced in half to show a jammy yolk, sits beside the pork. Two halves of bright green, blanched baby bok choy are tucked to the side. A small dollop of yellow karashi mustard rests on the rim. The dish is served on a dark walnut wood table with a pair of bamboo chopsticks on a ceramic rest. Natural side lighting highlights the glossy surface of the soy reduction. The entire plate is visible against a minimalist restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed short-grain white rice
Provide karashi mustard for heat
Pair with hot green tea
instructions: Sear pork cubes in a hot pan until browned on all sides.
Place pork in a pot with water, ginger, and scallions.
Simmer on low heat for 90 minutes.
Remove pork and discard simmering liquid and aromatics.
Return pork to the pot with soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar.
Braise on low heat for 45 minutes until the sauce reduces.
Add peeled eggs to the sauce for the final 5 minutes.
Ensure pork is tender and coated in a glossy glaze.
notes: Use a drop lid (otoshibuta) during braising to keep the pork submerged
Degrease the sauce before the final reduction for a cleaner flavor
The pork should be tender enough to break with chopsticks

recipes.recipe_name: Buta no Kakuni (Japanese Braised Pork Belly)
recipes.visual_description: Three large, glossy cubes of braised pork belly sit centered in a shallow, dark-glazed ceramic bowl. The pork skin is a deep mahogany color from the soy reduction. Next to the pork, a soft-boiled egg is halved lengthwise, revealing a jammy, vibrant orange yolk. Two vibrant green stalks of blanched bok choy provide a vertical element and color contrast. A thin pool of dark, translucent braising liquid surrounds the base. A small dollop of yellow karashi mustard rests on the rim. The setting includes a rustic wooden table, a side bowl of steamed white rice, and bamboo chopsticks on a ceramic rest. Natural side lighting highlights the succulent, glistening fat layers.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of steamed short-grain white rice
Provide karashi (Japanese hot mustard) for dipping
Pair with hot green tea or chilled sake
instructions: Cut pork belly into 5cm cubes.
Blanch cubes in boiling water for 5 minutes.
Drain and rinse pork under cold water.
Place pork in a heavy pot with dashi, sake, and ginger.
Simmer for 60 minutes using an otoshibuta or parchment lid.
Add soy sauce, mirin, and sugar.
Simmer for 45 minutes until meat is tender.
Remove pork and cool the liquid.
Skim solidified fat from the surface.
Reheat pork in the liquid and reduce until syrupy.
Serve in bowls with eggs and bok choy.
notes: Chilling the braising liquid overnight makes fat removal much easier.
Ensure the pork is fully submerged during the second simmer for even coloring.
Soft-boil eggs for exactly 6 minutes and 30 seconds for the perfect jammy yolk.

recipes.recipe_name: Charcoal-Crusted Chicken with Advocaat Cream
recipes.visual_description: A single whole chicken thigh, coated in a deep matte-black charcoal crust, sits at the center of a clean white porcelain plate. The chicken is seared crisp, showing a textured, dark surface. Surrounding the base is a smooth, pale gold advocaat and lemon reduction. Four 2cm cubes of almond tofu, pan-seared to a light golden brown, are placed around the chicken. Small fresh thyme leaves are scattered across the sauce for a vibrant green contrast. The plate sits on a light wood table in a modern bistro setting. Natural side lighting highlights the contrast between the black chicken and the creamy sauce. The composition is balanced with clean negative space, emphasizing the bold colors.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels.
Combine charcoal powder and sea salt in a small bowl.
Coat the chicken thighs evenly with the charcoal mixture.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken in the skillet.
Sear chicken for 6 to 8 minutes per side.
Confirm internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from pan and let rest.
Add minced shallots to the same skillet.
Sauté shallots for 2 minutes until translucent.
Pour in chicken stock and advocaat.
Whisk in lemon juice.
Simmer sauce for 4 minutes until thickened.
Cut almond tofu into 2cm cubes.
Sear tofu cubes in a separate non-stick pan until golden on all sides.
Place one whole chicken thigh on each plate.
Pour the advocaat sauce around the base of the chicken.
Top with pan-fried tofu cubes and fresh thyme.
notes: Use food-grade activated charcoal only.
Handle charcoal carefully as it stains surfaces easily.
Ensure the almond tofu is firm enough to pan-fry.

recipes.recipe_name: Mushroom and Green Bean Ragout with Strawberry-Glazed Vegetarian Sausage
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain plate set upon a light oak wood table. A thick, rectangular slice of golden-brown, butter-fried sourdough bread serves as the base. Resting on the bread is a rustic mound of sautéed cremini mushroom halves and vibrant, blanched green beans. Two whole, plump vegetarian sausages are positioned on top, coated in a glossy, dark red strawberry jam glaze that catches the light. Delicate shavings of pale yellow Gruyere cheese are scattered across the top, beginning to melt slightly. Fresh, bright red strawberry halves are tucked into the arrangement for color. The lighting is natural and soft, highlighting the contrast between the earthy mushrooms and the jewel-toned glaze. A simple linen napkin and silver fork sit to the side.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a chilled glass of dry rosé
Accompany with a simple arugula salad and lemon vinaigrette
instructions: Trim green beans and halve mushrooms.
Sauté mushrooms in 20g butter until deeply browned.
Blanch green beans in boiling water for 3 minutes and drain.
Add beans and vegetable stock to mushrooms.
Simmer until liquid reduces to a glaze.
Fry sourdough slices in remaining butter until golden and crisp.
Sear whole vegetarian sausages in olive oil until browned on all sides.
Whisk strawberry jam with 15ml water and add to sausage pan.
Coat sausages in the jam until a sticky glaze forms.
Place one fried bread slice on each plate.
Spoon the mushroom and green bean ragout over the bread.
Place two whole glazed sausages on top of the vegetables.
Shave Gruyere cheese over the warm dish.
Garnish with halved fresh strawberries and thyme leaves.
notes: Use smooth strawberry jam to ensure an even glaze on the sausages
Ensure the mushrooms are well-browned before adding stock for maximum umami flavor

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Indian Chicken Curry
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of chicken curry served in a traditional stainless steel bowl on a circular metal thali tray. The dish features large, tender chunks of bone-in chicken submerged in a thick, textured reddish-brown gravy. The sauce shows visible bits of softened onions and tomatoes. A generous handful of bright green chopped coriander is scattered over the top. Beside the bowl on the tray is a small mound of fluffy white basmati rice and two folded, charred whole wheat rotis. A side of raw red onion rings and a single green chili sit at the edge. The setting is a dark wooden table with warm, natural kitchen lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm roti or naan
Accompany with steamed basmati rice
Provide raw onion rings and lemon wedges on the side
Eat traditionally using the bread as a scoop for the chicken and gravy

ingredients.name: chicken thighs, bone-in, cut into large chunks

instructions: Heat oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Add cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 30 seconds.
Add onions. Sauté until deep golden brown.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add turmeric, chili powder, and coriander powder. Stir for 30 seconds.
Add tomato puree. Cook until oil separates from the spice mixture.
Add chicken chunks. Stir to coat thoroughly with the masala.
Pour in water and add salt. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 25 minutes.
Check chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Stir in garam masala. Turn off heat.
Garnish with chopped coriander before serving.
notes: For a spicier curry, add 2 slit green chilies with the ginger-garlic paste.
Ensure the onions are well-browned for a deep, authentic flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Peach and Lemon Verbena Entremet
recipes.visual_description: A single, high-gloss peach entremet sits off-center on a white porcelain plate with a delicate gold rim. The cake is perfectly spherical with a flat base, coated in a translucent, pale orange mirror glaze that reflects the soft, dramatic studio lighting. A clean vertical slice reveals the architectural interior: a crisp, golden-brown sable Breton base, a thick layer of airy white lemon verbena mousse, and a vibrant, concentrated center of orange-hued peach compote. The fruit is cut into precise 5mm cubes. A single, unpeeled peach wedge and one tiny micro-verbena leaf are placed with surgical precision on the top right. The background is a minimalist, cool white marble surface with significant negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a chilled glass of late-harvest Riesling
Use a formal silver dessert fork and spoon
Present on a chilled porcelain plate to maintain glaze integrity

ingredients.name: Heavy cream, whipped to soft peaks

instructions: Mix flour, 50g sugar, and butter until sandy. Add 2 egg yolks. Mix until dough forms. Chill 1 hour.
Roll dough to 4mm thickness. Cut into 14cm circles. Bake at 170°C for 15 minutes. Cool completely.
Combine diced peaches and 30g sugar in a pan. Heat to 40°C. Whisk in pectin. Boil for 1 minute. Stir in lemon juice.
Pour compote into 12cm silicone molds. Freeze until solid.
Infuse lemon verbena in hot milk for 20 minutes. Strain.
Whisk 2 egg yolks with 40g sugar. Temper with hot milk. Cook to 82°C. Stir in bloomed gelatin.
Cool custard to 30°C. Gently fold in whipped cream.
Fill 16cm molds halfway with mousse. Press frozen peach compote into center. Add more mousse. Top with sable disc. Freeze 6 hours.
Boil peach puree, remaining sugar, and white chocolate. Add 1 bloomed gelatin sheet. Emulsify with immersion blender. Cool to 35°C.
Unmold frozen cakes. Place on wire rack. Pour glaze over cakes. Let set for 5 minutes.
Transfer to plates. Garnish with one fresh peach wedge and one verbena leaf.
notes: Ensure the mirror glaze is exactly 35°C before pouring to achieve the correct thickness.
Do not over-mix the mousse once the cream is added to maintain a light texture.
The peach compote must be completely frozen to ensure clean layers during assembly.

recipes.recipe_name: Parmesan and Honey Shortbread
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of three thick Parmesan shortbread cookies is presented on a rustic cream-colored ceramic plate. The cookies are cut into 5 cm rounds with slightly textured, crumbly edges and a pale golden-brown finish. Small toasted specks of cheese are visible throughout the dough. The cookies are stacked casually in the center of the plate. A generous cluster of coarsely chopped walnut pieces sits atop the stack. Thick, glossy amber honey is drizzled over the walnuts, flowing naturally down the sides. The plate rests on a dark, weathered wooden table alongside a simple linen napkin. Soft, warm kitchen lighting emphasizes the matte texture of the shortbread and the shine of the honey.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small cup of strong espresso
Pair with a glass of sweet Vin Santo or Moscato
Enjoy as a 'dolce' after a light Mediterranean meal
instructions: Preheat oven to 170°C.
Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Whisk flour, sugar, and salt in a bowl.
Rub cold butter into flour until texture resembles breadcrumbs.
Add grated Parmesan and vanilla extract.
Knead briefly until a firm dough forms.
Roll dough to 1 cm thickness on a floured surface.
Cut into 5 cm circles using a round cutter.
Place rounds on the baking tray.
Bake for 15 minutes until light golden brown.
Cool completely on a wire rack.
Top each cookie with chopped walnuts and a honey drizzle before serving.
notes: Use aged Parmigiano Reggiano for the best flavor profile
Ensure the butter is very cold to maintain a flaky texture
Do not over-bake; the cookies should remain pale

recipes.recipe_name: Biff Rydberg
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Biff Rydberg served on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish features three distinct, neat mounds: crispy 1.5cm golden-brown potato cubes, deeply caramelized finely diced yellow onions, and seared 2cm beef tenderloin chunks with a dark savory crust. The meat is presented as whole, succulent cubes. A small, elegant pool of thick, pale mustard cream sauce rests at the side. Finely chopped fresh parsley is scattered over the top. The arrangement is organized yet organic, set on a light oak bistro table with a white cotton napkin and polished flatware. Natural window light emphasizes the contrast between the tender meat and crunchy potatoes, showing the entire plate with balanced negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a raw egg yolk in a half-shell nestled in the center
Accompany with pickled beets and freshly grated horseradish
Serve with a cold Swedish lager
instructions: Peel potatoes and cut into 1.5cm cubes.
Boil potato cubes in salted water for 5 minutes. Drain and pat dry.
Finely dice the onions.
Sauté onions in 15g butter over medium heat until dark brown and caramelized. Set aside.
Fry potatoes in oil and 20g butter until golden and crispy. Season with salt. Set aside.
Cut beef into 2cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Sear beef in a very hot pan with remaining butter and oil. Cook 2-3 minutes until browned. Keep medium-rare.
Simmer cream in a small saucepan until reduced by half. Whisk in mustard.
Place beef, potatoes, and onions in three separate mounds on the plate.
Drizzle mustard cream sauce over the beef or serve on the side.
notes: Ensure the pan is smoking hot before adding beef to achieve a proper crust
Pat potatoes completely dry before frying to ensure maximum crispiness
Do not mix the components on the plate before serving; the separation is traditional

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Pork Belly with Holy Basil (Moo Krob Pad Krapow)
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Thai Moo Krob served in a shallow, matte-finished ceramic bowl on a dark teak wood table. The dish features thick, 3cm cubes of golden-brown crispy pork belly, with the skin visibly blistered and crunchy. The meat is coated in a glossy, dark savory sauce with vibrant green holy basil leaves and bright red chili fragments scattered throughout. Beside the bowl sits a separate small white porcelain bowl of fluffy steamed jasmine rice. A traditional Thai brass spoon and fork rest on a folded linen napkin. The background is a soft-focus modern bistro setting with natural side lighting highlighting the glistening pork skin and fresh herb textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Prik Nam Pla (fish sauce with sliced chilies)
Accompany with a crispy fried egg with a runny yolk
Eat using a spoon in the right hand and a fork in the left
instructions: Place pork belly in a pot of cold water. Bring to a boil. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Remove pork. Pat the skin completely dry with paper towels.
Prick the skin surface repeatedly with a fork or needle tool.
Rub vinegar into the skin. Coat with salt. Let dry for 1 hour.
Heat oil to 180°C in a wok. Place pork skin-side down.
Fry until skin is puffed and golden. Flip and cook meat for 5 minutes.
Remove pork. Rest for 10 minutes. Cut into 3cm thick cubes.
Pound garlic and chilies into a coarse paste using a mortar and pestle.
Heat 15ml oil in a clean wok. Sauté garlic-chili paste until fragrant.
Add pork cubes, oyster sauce, soy sauces, and sugar. Toss over high heat.
Turn off heat. Fold in holy basil leaves until just wilted.
notes: Ensure the pork skin is bone-dry before frying to achieve maximum crunch
Holy basil is distinct from Thai sweet basil; it has a peppery, clove-like flavor
Do not overcook the basil or it will lose its aromatic oils

recipes.recipe_name: Moroccan Lamb Tagine with Apricots
recipes.visual_description: The dish features large, 4cm chunks of tender lamb shoulder coated in a thick, mahogany-colored sauce. Bright orange halves of fresh apricots are nestled naturally between the meat chunks, showing soft, caramelized edges from the gentle braise. Whole blanched almonds provide a pale, matte contrast against the glossy sauce. A scatter of vibrant green chopped cilantro adds freshness. The meal is presented in a traditional terracotta tagine base on a dark wooden table. A side bowl of fluffy, steamed couscous with a silver spoon sits nearby. The lighting is warm and natural, highlighting the rich textures of the meat and the velvety surface of the apricots.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed couscous or crusty khobz bread
Accompany with Moroccan mint tea
Present in a traditional ceramic tagine vessel

ingredients.name: Saffron threads, soaked in 50ml warm water

instructions: Heat oil in a heavy-based pot or tagine over medium-high heat.
Brown lamb chunks in batches. Remove and set aside.
Sauté onions in the same pot for 8 minutes until soft.
Add garlic, ginger, Ras el Hanout, and cinnamon. Stir for 1 minute.
Return lamb to the pot. Add saffron water and lamb stock.
Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook on low heat for 90 minutes.
Stir in dried apricots and honey. Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes.
Gently place fresh apricot halves on top. Cover and cook for 5 minutes.
Ensure sauce is thick and glossy. Season with salt and pepper.
Top with toasted almonds and fresh cilantro before serving.
notes: Ensure the lamb is fork-tender before adding fresh apricots
Do not overcook fresh apricots to maintain their shape
Toast almonds until just golden for maximum nuttiness

recipes.recipe_name: Black Pepper Beef Medallions with Roasted Asparagus
recipes.visual_description: A single thick beef medallion sits prominently on a large, clean white porcelain plate. The beef is seared to a deep mahogany brown with a visible crust of coarse-cracked black pepper. It is topped with a silky, light-brown shallot cream sauce. Beside the beef, a bundle of vibrant green roasted asparagus spears lies in a neat, parallel arrangement, showing light charring at the tips. Tiny flecks of translucent minced shallot and garlic are scattered within the glossy sauce. The setting is a dark oak bistro table with a folded grey cotton napkin and polished silver cutlery. Natural side lighting creates soft shadows, emphasizing the succulent texture of the whole, unsliced meat and the crispness of the vegetables.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of robust red wine such as Cabernet Sauvignon
Accompany with crusty baguette slices to soak up the peppercorn sauce
instructions: Season beef medallions generously with salt and 10g of cracked black pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat.
Place beef in the hot skillet. Sear for 4 minutes per side for medium-rare.
Remove beef from the pan. Transfer to a warm plate to rest.
Toss asparagus spears with remaining 15ml olive oil and a pinch of salt.
Roast asparagus in a 200°C oven for 8 minutes until tender-crisp and lightly charred.
Add butter to the beef skillet over medium heat.
Sauté minced shallots and garlic for 2 minutes until translucent.
Pour beef stock into the skillet. Scrape the bottom to release browned bits.
Simmer stock until reduced by half.
Stir in heavy cream and the remaining 5g of cracked black pepper.
Simmer for 2 minutes until the sauce thickens to a coating consistency.
Place one whole beef medallion on each plate.
Arrange a bundle of roasted asparagus spears alongside the beef.
Spoon the warm peppercorn sauce over the beef medallions.
notes: Ensure the skillet is very hot before adding beef to achieve a proper crust.
Cracking peppercorns fresh provides significantly better flavor and texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Moroccan Lamb Tagine with Raisins
recipes.visual_description: The dish features four large, succulent chunks of braised lamb shoulder coated in a glossy, mahogany-colored sauce. Plump dark and golden raisins are scattered throughout the sauce, providing jewel-like highlights. The lamb is presented in a traditional terracotta tagine base on a rustic wooden table. A scattering of whole, pale golden toasted almonds and bright green cilantro leaves provides color contrast. To the side, a small ceramic bowl holds a mound of fluffy, pale yellow couscous. The lighting is soft and natural, emphasizing the moist texture of the meat and the sheen of the reduction. A clean white cotton napkin and a traditional Moroccan spoon are placed neatly beside the vessel.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fluffy couscous or crusty khobz bread
Pair with a side of Moroccan mint tea
Present in a communal tagine for traditional family-style dining
instructions: Heat olive oil in a heavy-based pot or tagine over medium-high heat.
Brown lamb chunks in batches until seared on all sides. Remove and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Sauté onions for 8 minutes until translucent.
Add garlic, fresh ginger, cinnamon, cumin, ground ginger, and turmeric. Stir for 1 minute.
Return lamb to the pot. Add stock, saffron, and honey.
Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook on low heat for 90 minutes.
Stir in all raisins. Continue simmering covered for 30 minutes until lamb is tender.
Remove lid. Simmer for 10 minutes to thicken the sauce into a glaze.
Garnish with toasted almonds and fresh cilantro before serving.
notes: Do not trim all the fat from the lamb as it provides essential flavor during the long braise.
If the sauce is too thin, remove the meat and boil the liquid rapidly for 5 minutes.

recipes.recipe_name: Moroccan Lamb Tagine with Cotton Candy
recipes.visual_description: A deep terracotta tagine sits on a dark wooden bistro table. The center features large, tender chunks of braised lamb shoulder glistening in a rich, dark amber sauce flecked with golden saffron and plump chickpeas. The meat is served as whole chunks, not sliced. Resting directly atop the warm lamb is a delicate, airy mound of white cotton candy, resembling a soft, spun-sugar cloud. Vibrant green cilantro leaves are scattered around the base of the lamb. The lighting is warm and natural, highlighting the contrast between the moist meat and the dry, crystalline sugar strands. A side of fluffy couscous in a small white porcelain bowl and a traditional silver spoon complete the professional restaurant presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm couscous or crusty khobz bread
Accompany with a side of harissa for heat
Traditional Moroccan mint tea service follows the meal
instructions: Heat oil in a large heavy-based pot over medium-high heat.
Season lamb chunks with salt and pepper.
Sear lamb in batches until browned on all sides.
Remove lamb and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium.
Add onions to the pot and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in garlic, ginger, cumin, coriander, and cinnamon.
Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return lamb to the pot.
Add stock and saffron.
Bring to a simmer and cover tightly.
Cook on low heat for 90 minutes or until lamb is tender.
Stir in chickpeas and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes to thicken sauce.
Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Divide lamb and sauce into four bowls.
Top each portion with a fresh mound of cotton candy immediately before serving.
notes: The cotton candy acts as the traditional sweet element found in Moroccan tagines.
Place the cotton candy on the dish at the table to ensure it does not melt prematurely.
Ensure the lamb reaches an internal temperature of at least 75°C.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Pork Belly with Angelica Root
recipes.visual_description: Four large, uniform cubes of braised pork belly sit centered in a shallow, dark-glazed ceramic bowl. The skin is translucent and deeply caramelized to a mahogany hue, shimmering with a thick, glossy reduction. A single, thin slice of rehydrated angelica root rests atop the meat. The pork is surrounded by a pool of dark, silken sauce. Bright green blanched bok choy halves are tucked neatly to one side for color contrast. The dish is served on a light-colored wooden table with a side of steamed jasmine rice in a small white porcelain bowl and dark wood chopsticks. Natural side lighting highlights the gelatinous texture of the fat and the rich sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice
Accompany with hot Oolong tea
Provide a small side of pickled mustard greens
instructions: Place pork cubes in a pot of cold water. Bring to a boil for 5 minutes. Drain and rinse pork.
Heat a wok over medium heat. Add pork cubes. Sear until fat renders and edges turn golden.
Add rock sugar. Stir until melted and light brown.
Deglaze with Shaoxing wine. Add light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, ginger, scallions, and star anise.
Pour in water. Add angelica root slices.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 90 minutes until pork is tender.
Remove cover. Increase heat to high. Reduce sauce until thick and glossy.
Discard ginger, scallions, and star anise before serving.
notes: Do not overcook the angelica root as it can become overly bitter.
Rock sugar provides a superior glossy sheen compared to granulated sugar.

recipes.recipe_name: Moroccan Lamb Tagine with Raisins
recipes.visual_description: The dish features four large, succulent chunks of braised lamb shoulder coated in a glossy, mahogany-colored sauce. Plump dark and golden raisins are scattered throughout the sauce, providing jewel-like highlights. The lamb is presented in a traditional terracotta tagine base on a rustic wooden table. A scattering of whole, pale golden toasted almonds and bright green cilantro leaves provides color contrast. To the side, a small ceramic bowl holds a mound of fluffy, pale yellow couscous. The lighting is soft and natural, emphasizing the moist texture of the meat and the sheen of the reduction. A clean white cotton napkin and a traditional Moroccan spoon are placed neatly beside the vessel.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fluffy couscous or crusty khobz bread
Pair with a side of Moroccan mint tea
Present in a communal tagine for traditional family-style dining
instructions: Heat olive oil in a heavy-based pot or tagine over medium-high heat.
Brown lamb chunks in batches until seared on all sides. Remove and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Sauté onions for 8 minutes until translucent.
Add garlic, fresh ginger, cinnamon, cumin, ground ginger, and turmeric. Stir for 1 minute.
Return lamb to the pot. Add stock, saffron, and honey.
Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook on low heat for 90 minutes.
Stir in all raisins. Continue simmering covered for 30 minutes until lamb is tender.
Remove lid. Simmer for 10 minutes to thicken the sauce into a glaze.
Garnish with toasted almonds and fresh cilantro before serving.
notes: Do not trim all the fat from the lamb as it provides essential flavor during the long braise.
If the sauce is too thin, remove the meat and boil the liquid rapidly for 5 minutes.

recipes.recipe_name: Gochujang Chicken and Sweet Potato Soup
recipes.visual_description: A deep, vibrant red gochujang broth fills a matte black stone bowl, centered on a light oak table. The camera captures the entire bowl and surrounding modern bistro table setting. Submerged are 3cm chunks of succulent chicken thigh and 2.5cm cubes of tender sweet potato. A cluster of delicate white enoki mushrooms rests on the surface, their long stems partially submerged. Finely sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds provide a fresh contrast. The arrangement is natural and rustic, showcasing the hearty textures of the braised ingredients. A pair of stainless steel chopsticks and a traditional long-handled spoon lie on a linen napkin beside the bowl. Natural daylight highlights the glossy surface of the savory broth and the soft steam.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a bowl of steamed short-grain white rice
Accompany with small dishes of kimchi and pickled radish
Eat using traditional Korean stainless steel chopsticks and a long-handled spoon
instructions: Cut chicken into 3cm chunks.
Peel and cube sweet potatoes into 2.5cm pieces.
Mince garlic and grate ginger.
Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Brown chicken chunks for 5 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger. Stir for 1 minute.
Add gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, and mirin.
Pour in water. Stir in MSG.
Bring the liquid to a boil.
Add sweet potato cubes.
Reduce heat to medium. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature is 75°C.
Add trimmed enoki mushrooms. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Garnish with sliced green onions.
Serve immediately.
notes: Use chicken thighs for maximum tenderness during simmering
Adjust the amount of gochugaru to control the heat level
Ensure sweet potatoes are cut uniformly for even cooking

recipes.recipe_name: Traditional Shakshuka
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a seasoned 25cm cast iron skillet centered on a rustic dark wood table. The base is a thick, vibrant red tomato and red bell pepper sauce, showing visible chunks of softened onion and charred pepper skins. Eight large eggs are poached directly in the sauce, spaced evenly with firm whites and glistening, runny yellow yolks kept perfectly whole. Bright white crumbles of feta cheese are scattered across the surface. Freshly chopped green cilantro and flat-leaf parsley provide a vivid color contrast. A side of warm, charred pita bread triangles sits on a small ceramic plate. The lighting is bright and natural, highlighting the steam rising from the savory sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly in the cooking skillet for communal dining
Accompany with warm pita bread or challah for dipping
Pair with a side of Israeli salad or hummus
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onion and bell pepper. Sauté 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in garlic, cumin, paprika, and cayenne. Cook 1 minute.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Season with salt and pepper.
Simmer sauce for 15 minutes until thickened.
Use a spoon to make 8 small wells in the sauce.
Crack one egg into each well. Cover the skillet.
Cook 5 to 8 minutes until egg whites are set but yolks remain runny.
Remove from heat. Top with crumbled feta and cilantro.
Serve immediately from the skillet.
notes: Do not overcook the eggs; the yolks must remain liquid to create a rich sauce.
Fresh tomatoes can be substituted for canned if very ripe.

recipes.recipe_name: Sweet Onion Ice Cream with Balsamic Caramel
recipes.special_requests: I want this to be an onion ice cream
recipes.visual_description: A single large, perfectly smooth scoop of pale mauve onion ice cream sits in the center of a chilled white porcelain bowl. The ice cream has a matte, velvety texture with a subtle sheen. A thick, dark mahogany balsamic reduction is drizzled in a clean, deliberate motion over the top, pooling slightly at the base of the scoop. Beside the ice cream, three small cubes of honey-glazed roasted red onion provide a textural contrast and visual interest. The color palette features sophisticated dusty rose and deep brown tones. The dish is presented on a dark wood table with a crisp white cotton napkin. Soft, natural lighting highlights the smooth curves of the scoop and the viscous, glossy syrup.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a chilled porcelain bowl
Accompany with a small glass of aged dessert wine
instructions: Sauté sliced onions in butter over low heat until soft.
Add 30g sugar to onions. Cook until deeply caramelized and jam-like.
Combine milk and cream in a saucepan. Add caramelized onions.
Bring mixture to a simmer. Remove from heat. Cover and steep for 30 minutes.
Strain mixture through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard onion solids.
Whisk egg yolks with 70g sugar until pale and thick.
Slowly pour warm onion cream into yolks while whisking constantly.
Return mixture to saucepan. Stir over low heat until custard reaches 82°C.
Chill custard in an ice bath. Refrigerate until completely cold.
Churn in an ice cream maker according to manufacturer instructions.
Simmer balsamic vinegar with remaining 50g sugar until reduced by half.
Serve one large scoop of ice cream drizzled with balsamic syrup.
notes: Ensure the onions are fully caramelized to remove all sulfurous bite
Strain the custard twice for the smoothest possible texture

recipes.recipe_name: Chinese Stir-fried Tomato and Egg
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chinese Stir-fried Tomato and Egg is presented in a shallow white porcelain bowl. The dish features large, tender golden-yellow egg curds mixed with softened, vibrant red tomato wedges. The tomatoes are cut into thick 3cm wedges and slightly caramelized, releasing a rich, glossy orange-red sauce that coats the egg chunks. Finely sliced green scallion rings are scattered across the surface. The bowl sits on a dark walnut wood table. To the side, a small white ceramic bowl contains fluffy steamed jasmine rice. A pair of dark wood chopsticks rests on a ceramic holder. Natural daylight creates soft shadows, highlighting the silky texture of the eggs and the moisture of the tomatoes.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice
Accompany with a side of chili oil
Traditional family-style presentation

ingredients.name: Ripe Roma tomatoes, cut into 3cm wedges
Scallions, whites and greens separated and sliced

instructions: Whisk eggs with salt and Shaoxing wine in a bowl until combined.
Heat 30ml oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Pour in eggs and scramble into large curds for 30 seconds until 80% set.
Remove eggs from wok and set aside.
Add remaining 15ml oil to the wok.
Stir-fry scallion whites and ginger for 10 seconds.
Add tomato wedges and stir-fry for 2 minutes until softened.
Add sugar, soy sauce, and water to the tomatoes.
Cover and simmer for 1 minute to create a thick sauce.
Return eggs to the wok and toss gently to combine with tomatoes.
Drizzle with sesame oil and remove from heat.
Garnish with scallion greens.
notes: Ensure the wok is very hot before adding eggs to achieve proper puffiness.
Do not over-scramble the eggs; keep them in large, soft chunks.
Adjust sugar based on the natural acidity of the tomatoes.

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Grilled Beef Salad
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion of Thai Grilled Beef Salad sits on a rustic ceramic plate. The beef is cut into 2cm chunks, revealing a juicy medium-rare interior and a dark, seared crust. These chunks are tossed with thin slices of purple shallots, bright green mint leaves, and fresh cilantro. A fine dusting of toasted rice powder provides a gritty, golden texture over the meat. The dish is presented on a well-used wooden table next to a traditional woven bamboo sticky rice container. A small side of raw cabbage wedges and long beans adds a crisp element. Warm, natural kitchen lighting highlights the glistening lime-based dressing. The plating is casual and authentic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm sticky rice in a bamboo basket
Provide fresh raw cabbage wedges to balance heat
Include long beans and Thai basil on the side
instructions: Season beef with salt.
Heat a heavy pan over high heat.
Sear beef for 3 minutes per side.
Remove beef and rest for 5 minutes.
Cut beef into 2cm chunks.
Whisk fish sauce, lime juice, and sugar in a bowl.
Stir in chili flakes and toasted rice powder.
Add beef chunks and sliced shallots to the bowl.
Toss until ingredients are well coated.
Fold in mint and cilantro leaves gently.
Serve immediately while beef is warm.
notes: Toast raw glutinous rice in a dry pan until dark brown before grinding for the powder
Ensure the pan is smoking hot before searing beef
Adjust chili flakes to personal heat preference

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef with Tomato and Basil
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of braised beef served in a shallow white porcelain pasta bowl. Three large, 5cm chunks of tender, dark-seared beef are positioned centrally, coated in a thick, glossy red tomato sauce. Vibrant 2cm carrot rounds and translucent diced onions are scattered naturally around the meat. The dish is garnished with three whole, bright green basil leaves and a visible sprinkle of coarse black pepper. The plate sits on a dark oak table in a modern bistro setting. A side of crusty ciabatta bread rests on a small wooden board. Natural side lighting emphasizes the rich, fibrous texture of the beef and the sauce's sheen, with moderate negative space around the rim.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for scarpetta
Pair with a medium-bodied red wine like Chianti
Serve in wide, shallow bowls

ingredients.name: Beef chuck roast, cut into 5cm chunks

instructions: Pat beef chunks dry with paper towels.
Season beef generously with salt and half of the black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-based pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks in batches until deep brown on all sides.
Remove beef from pot and set aside.
Add diced onions and carrot rounds to the pot.
Sauté for 6 minutes until onions are translucent.
Add minced garlic and remaining black pepper. Stir for 1 minute.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and beef stock. Deglaze the pot bottom.
Return beef to the pot. Ensure liquid half-covers the meat.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 2.5 hours until meat is fork-tender.
Stir in torn basil leaves immediately before serving.
notes: Do not trim all the fat from the beef as it adds richness to the sauce
If sauce is too thin, simmer uncovered for the last 15 minutes
Fresh basil must be added at the end to preserve its aromatic oils

recipes.recipe_name: Chinese Tomato and Egg Stir-fry
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a shallow, white porcelain rimmed bowl, showcasing a vibrant contrast between glossy, bright red tomato wedges and large, fluffy clouds of golden-yellow scrambled eggs. The tomatoes are cut into uniform wedges, softened into a thick, shimmering savory-sweet sauce that coats every element. Scattered across the top are bright green, bias-cut scallion rounds. The arrangement is natural and fluid, filling the center of the bowl with moderate negative space around the rim. The setting features a dark wood table, a pair of polished dark wood chopsticks on a ceramic holder, and a small side bowl of steamed jasmine rice. Natural side-lighting highlights the silky texture of the eggs and the reflective glaze of the tomato sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed long-grain jasmine rice
Accompany with a side of quickly blanched bok choy
Provide chopsticks and a short-handled ceramic soup spoon

ingredients.name: Ripe Roma tomatoes, cut into 8 wedges each
Scallions, white and green parts separated and sliced

instructions: Whisk eggs with Shaoxing wine and salt until well combined.
Heat 30ml oil in a wok over high heat until shimmering.
Pour in eggs. Stir gently until puffed and just set. Remove eggs immediately.
Add remaining oil to the wok. Sauté ginger, garlic, and scallion whites for 30 seconds.
Add tomato wedges. Stir-fry until skins begin to soften and juices release.
Stir in soy sauce and sugar. Simmer for 1 minute.
Pour in cornstarch slurry. Stir until sauce thickens and becomes glossy.
Return eggs to the wok. Fold gently to combine without breaking the egg clouds.
Drizzle with sesame oil. Garnish with scallion greens.
Serve immediately with steamed jasmine rice.
notes: Use very ripe tomatoes for maximum juice and flavor.
Do not overcook the eggs in the first step; they should remain soft and custardy.
Adjust sugar based on the natural acidity of the tomatoes.

recipes.recipe_name: Jeonbok-Sotbap (Abalone and Shiitake Pot Rice)
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a traditional black stone pot centered on a dark wooden trivet. The short-grain rice is glistening and slightly green-tinted from the sautéed abalone guts. On top of the rice, thick 2cm chunks of golden-seared abalone and 5mm thick earthy brown shiitake mushroom slices are arranged in a natural, rustic cluster. Bright green sliced scallions and golden sesame seeds are scattered over the center. The scene includes a pair of stainless steel Korean chopsticks and a long-handled spoon resting on a white ceramic holder. A small side dish of red Napa cabbage kimchi provides a color contrast. The lighting is soft and natural, emphasizing the textures of the seafood and mushrooms.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Yangnyeom-jang (seasoned soy sauce) for individual seasoning.
Provide Baechu-kimchi as a fermented palate cleanser.
Present in the cooking pot to maintain heat throughout the meal.
instructions: Wash rice until water runs clear. Drain for 30 minutes.
Clean abalones. Remove meat from shells. Detach guts.
Finely mince the abalone guts. Set aside.
Cut abalone meat into 2cm thick chunks. Score the surface lightly.
Remove shiitake stems. Slice caps into 5mm thick pieces.
Melt butter in a heavy-bottomed stone or ceramic pot over medium heat.
Sauté minced guts and garlic for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add drained rice. Stir-fry for 3 minutes until grains are coated and translucent.
Pour in dashima stock, soy sauce, and mirin. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 10 minutes.
Place abalone chunks and shiitake slices on top of the rice.
Cover pot. Cook on low for 5 minutes.
Turn off heat. Let the pot sit covered for 5 minutes to steam.
Drizzle with sesame oil. Top with green onions and sesame seeds.
notes: Use the freshest abalone possible for the best flavor from the guts.
Do not open the lid during the final steaming phase to ensure even rice texture.
Scrape the bottom of the pot at the end to enjoy the 'nurungji' (scorched rice).

recipes.recipe_name: Poulet au Vinaigre
recipes.visual_description: The dish features two whole, golden-brown bone-in chicken thighs placed centrally on a wide-rimmed white porcelain plate. The chicken skin is crisp and glistening with a light amber sheen from the vinegar reduction. A rich, translucent sauce pools around the base of the chicken, containing visible small red tomato cubes and finely minced green tarragon. The plate is set on a dark oak bistro table next to a folded white cotton napkin and polished silver cutlery. Natural side-lighting highlights the texture of the seared skin and the glossy, emulsified sauce. Moderate negative space ensures a clean, professional restaurant presentation, focusing entirely on the textures of the braised poultry.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed white rice or crusty baguette
Accompany with a glass of dry white wine
Present in a shallow wide bowl for sauce retention
instructions: Season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down in the pan.
Sear for 8 minutes until skin is golden and crisp.
Flip chicken and cook for 5 minutes.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Drain excess fat, leaving 15 ml in the pan.
Add diced shallots and garlic to the pan.
Sauté for 2 minutes until translucent.
Deglaze the pan with white wine vinegar.
Scrape all browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Reduce vinegar by half over medium heat.
Add diced tomatoes and chicken stock.
Return chicken to the pan, skin-side up.
Simmer for 20 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C internally.
Transfer chicken to a warm serving plate.
Whisk cold butter into the simmering sauce to emulsify.
Stir in chopped tarragon.
Pour the finished sauce over the chicken thighs.
notes: Use high-quality aged white wine vinegar for a smoother acidity profile.
Ensure chicken skin remains above the liquid line during simmering to maintain crispness.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tomato and Pepper Pan Hash
recipes.special_requests: Needs to be fried in a saucepan and eaten from the saucepan itself
recipes.visual_description: A well-used stainless steel saucepan sits centrally on a rustic wooden table. The pan is filled with a thick, hearty hash featuring 2cm diced red peppers and softened onions. The sauce is a rich, creamy orange-red color derived from vegetable stock, flour, and tomatoes. Visible chunks of cooked tomato are dispersed throughout the mixture. Coarse black pepper is sprinkled generously over the top. A swirl of white mayonnaise creates a distinct marbled effect across the glossy surface. Four metal spoons are placed around the rim of the pan for communal eating. The lighting is warm and domestic, highlighting the natural textures and vibrant colors of the sautéed vegetables within the pan.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the cooking saucepan
Provide a loaf of crusty bread for dipping
Eat communally with spoons
instructions: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add diced onions and red peppers to the pan.
Fry for 8 minutes until vegetables soften and edges brown slightly.
Add minced garlic and fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in flour and cook for 2 minutes while stirring constantly.
Add chopped tomatoes and black pepper.
Pour in vegetable stock slowly while stirring to prevent lumps.
Simmer for 10 minutes until the sauce reaches a thick consistency.
Remove the saucepan from the heat.
Fold in the mayonnaise until the sauce is creamy and marbled.
Place the saucepan directly on the table for communal serving.
notes: Ensure the flour cooks for at least two minutes to remove the raw taste
Stir the stock in gradually to maintain a smooth sauce texture
Adjust black pepper to taste for more heat

recipes.recipe_name: Hungarian Beef Goulash
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl on a dark oak table. The focus is a hearty portion of Hungarian beef stew. The beef is cut into 3cm chunks, appearing dark red and tender. Vibrant orange carrots are cut into 2cm rounds. Potatoes are 2cm cubes, absorbing the deep red sauce. The sauce is thick and glossy, colored intensely by sweet paprika. Red bell peppers are cut into 2cm squares. A single dollop of white sour cream is placed on the side. A sprig of fresh parsley is the garnish. A side of crusty rye bread rests on a small ceramic plate next to the bowl. Natural light creates soft shadows and highlights the rich textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Galuska or Nokedli dumplings
Accompany with pickled cucumbers or fermented cabbage
Provide thick slices of fresh rye bread for dipping
instructions: Cut beef into 3cm chunks.
Finely dice onions and mince garlic.
Cut carrots into 2cm rounds and potatoes into 2cm cubes.
Dice tomatoes and cut bell pepper into 2cm squares.
Heat lard in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Sauté onions until translucent and golden.
Remove pot from heat and stir in paprika and caraway seeds.
Add beef chunks and return to heat.
Sear meat for 5 minutes until browned.
Add garlic, tomatoes, and bell pepper.
Pour in beef stock and add bay leaf.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 90 minutes.
Add potatoes and carrots.
Simmer for 30 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and pepper.
notes: Do not boil the paprika over high heat to avoid bitterness.
The stew is even better when reheated the next day.
Ensure the beef is chuck or a similar braising cut for tenderness.

recipes.recipe_name: Jeonbok-Sotbap (Abalone and Shiitake Pot Rice)
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a traditional black stone pot centered on a dark wooden trivet. The short-grain rice is glistening and slightly green-tinted from the sautéed abalone guts. On top of the rice, thick 2cm chunks of golden-seared abalone and 5mm thick earthy brown shiitake mushroom slices are arranged in a natural, rustic cluster. Bright green sliced scallions and golden sesame seeds are scattered over the center. The scene includes a pair of stainless steel Korean chopsticks and a long-handled spoon resting on a white ceramic holder. A small side dish of red Napa cabbage kimchi provides a color contrast. The lighting is soft and natural, emphasizing the textures of the seafood and mushrooms.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Yangnyeom-jang (seasoned soy sauce) for individual seasoning.
Provide Baechu-kimchi as a fermented palate cleanser.
Present in the cooking pot to maintain heat throughout the meal.

Clean abalones. Remove meat from shells. Detach guts.
Finely mince the abalone guts. Set aside.
Cut abalone meat into 2cm thick chunks. Score the surface lightly.
Remove shiitake stems. Slice caps into 5mm thick pieces.
Melt butter in a heavy-bottomed stone or ceramic pot over medium heat.
Sauté minced guts and garlic for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add drained rice. Stir-fry for 3 minutes until grains are coated and translucent.
Pour in dashima stock, soy sauce, and mirin. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 10 minutes.
Place abalone chunks and shiitake slices on top of the rice.
Cover pot. Cook on low for 5 minutes.
Turn off heat. Let the pot sit covered for 5 minutes to steam.
Drizzle with sesame oil. Top with green onions and sesame seeds.

Scrape the bottom of the pot at the end to enjoy the 'nurungji' (scorched rice).

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Roasted Celeriac Steaks with Melted Sulguni
recipes.visual_description: A single, thick 3cm round celeriac steak is centered on a matte white porcelain plate. The celeriac features deep golden-brown caramelized edges. A thick, molten layer of ivory-white Sulguni cheese blankets the top, showing small toasted brown spots from the oven's heat. Coarsely chopped brown walnuts and vibrant green cilantro are scattered across the cheese. The plate rests on a dark oak bistro table next to a folded gray cotton napkin and a traditional Georgian wine glass. Natural side lighting highlights the fibrous roasted texture of the root and the glossy, elastic pull of the melted cheese. Moderate negative space surrounds the centerpiece, creating a clean, professional restaurant presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Shoti bread
Pair with a dry amber (Qvevri) wine
Accompany with pickled jonjoli or cucumbers
instructions: Peel the celeriac. Cut into 3cm thick round steaks.
Heat sunflower oil in a large heavy skillet over medium-high heat.
Season celeriac rounds with salt and pepper.
Sear celeriac for 5 minutes per side until deep golden brown.
Add butter and smashed garlic to the pan. Baste steaks with foaming butter for 2 minutes.
Transfer skillet to a 200°C oven. Roast for 15-20 minutes until tender.
Slice sulguni cheese into 1cm thick pieces.
Place cheese slabs on each celeriac steak. Return to oven for 3-5 minutes until melted and bubbly.
Top with chopped walnuts and cilantro before serving.
notes: Ensure the celeriac is fully tender by piercing with a knife before adding cheese.
Sulguni is salty; adjust additional seasoning accordingly.
High-smoke point sunflower oil is essential for the initial sear.

recipes.recipe_name: Spaghetti with Zucchini and Pecorino Romano
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of spaghetti sits in a shallow, rustic cream-colored ceramic bowl. The pasta is coated in a glossy, translucent Pecorino emulsion. Deeply browned, thin zucchini rounds are folded throughout the noodles. Blistered, halved cherry tomatoes provide bright red accents against the golden-green vegetables. The dish is topped with a light dusting of finely grated Pecorino and three small, torn basil leaves. The bowl rests on a dark, well-worn wooden table next to a folded linen napkin and a simple stainless steel fork. Soft, warm kitchen lighting highlights the oily sheen of the pasta and the charred edges of the zucchini. The entire plate is visible, showing a modest, home-style portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while the cheese emulsion is fluid
Pair with a crisp white wine from the Campania region
Provide extra grated Pecorino Romano at the table
instructions: Boil a large pot of salted water.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry zucchini rounds in batches until golden brown on both sides.
Remove zucchini and set aside on a plate.
Add garlic and cherry tomatoes to the same skillet.
Sauté 3 minutes until tomatoes soften and blister.
Cook spaghetti in boiling water until 2 minutes before al dente.
Reserve 250ml of pasta cooking water.
Drain pasta and add to the skillet with tomatoes.
Add fried zucchini and 150ml of reserved pasta water to the skillet.
Toss over medium heat for 1 minute.
Remove skillet from heat.
Add Pecorino Romano and remaining pasta water.
Stir vigorously to create a creamy emulsion.
Garnish with torn basil and black pepper.
notes: Do not add cheese while the pan is on the heat to prevent clumping
The starch in the pasta water is essential for the creamy sauce texture
Zucchini should be well-browned for maximum flavor

recipes.recipe_name: Vietnamese Black Pepper Shaking Beef
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Shaking Beef served on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish features 2.5cm cubes of seared beef with a dark, glossy black pepper glaze. The beef chunks are piled naturally in the center, showing a caramelized crust. Interspersed are charred shallot quarters and vibrant red tomato wedges, softened but holding their shape. A bed of fresh green watercress sits beneath the meat. To the side, a perfectly shaped mound of fluffy white basmati rice is presented in a small ceramic bowl. A small condiment dish contains lime juice and cracked black pepper. The setting is a dark wood table with a pair of dark wood chopsticks and a white cotton napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small dish of lime juice and cracked black pepper
Place meat over a bed of fresh watercress
Use traditional dark wood chopsticks
instructions: Boil 450ml water.
Add rinsed basmati rice.
Cover and simmer 12 minutes.
Cut beef into 2.5cm cubes.
Whisk soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, and black pepper.
Marinate beef in half the sauce for 15 minutes.
Quarter the shallots.
Cut tomatoes into wedges.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Add beef cubes in a single layer.
Sear for 2 minutes without moving.
Add shallots and minced garlic.
Shake the wok constantly for 2 minutes.
Add tomatoes and remaining sauce.
Toss in butter to glaze the meat.
Remove from heat immediately.
notes: Ensure the wok is smoking hot before adding meat
Do not overcrowd the pan to ensure a proper sear
Use a high smoke point oil like peanut or canola

recipes.recipe_name: Steak au Poivre with Cognac Sauce
recipes.visual_description: One whole, thick-cut beef fillet steak sits centered on a clean white porcelain plate. The steak remains unsliced to preserve juices. A glossy, pale brown cognac cream sauce, speckled with coarse black peppercorns, coats the top and pools elegantly around the base. Beside the steak, golden-brown roasted potato wedges and vibrant green beans provide color contrast. The arrangement is organic and professional, utilizing moderate negative space. The setting features a modern bistro atmosphere with a dark wooden table, a crisp white cotton napkin, and polished silver flatware. Natural light accentuates the seared crust of the beef and the velvety texture of the sauce. The entire plate is captured in a balanced, realistic composition.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with traditional French pommes frites
Pair with a full-bodied Bordeaux red wine
Include crusty baguette slices to soak up the sauce
instructions: Crush peppercorns coarsely using a mortar and pestle.
Press crushed peppercorns firmly onto both sides of each steak.
Season steaks with sea salt.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed skillet over high heat.
Place steaks in the hot pan.
Sear steaks for 4 minutes per side for medium-rare.
Remove steaks from the pan and place on a warm plate.
Rest steaks for 5 minutes.
Discard excess fat from the skillet.
Add butter and diced shallots to the skillet.
Sauté shallots for 2 minutes until translucent.
Pour cognac into the pan.
Ignite cognac with a long match to flambé.
Let the flames subside naturally.
Add beef stock to the pan.
Boil liquid until reduced by half.
Stir in heavy cream.
Simmer sauce until it thickens enough to coat a spoon.
Return steaks and any accumulated juices to the pan.
Coat steaks with sauce and serve immediately.
notes: Use VSOP cognac for a deeper flavor profile
Ensure steaks reach room temperature before searing
Do not over-crush peppercorns to maintain texture

recipes.recipe_name: Serrano Ham and Honey Panna Cotta with Compressed Melon
recipes.visual_description: A single, cream-colored panna cotta sits centrally on a clean white porcelain plate. The panna cotta has a smooth, matte surface and a delicate wobble. On top, a cluster of vibrant orange cantaloupe cubes, precisely diced into 1cm squares, provides a sharp color contrast. Several large, jagged shards of honey-glazed, deep-burgundy Serrano ham are tucked into the melon, standing vertically to add height and a glossy, crystalline texture. Small, bright green mint leaves are placed asymmetrically around the fruit. The dish is presented in a modern bistro setting on a light oak table, illuminated by soft, natural side lighting that highlights the creamy texture and the crispness of the ham. A small, contemporary silver spoon rests on a folded white cotton napkin to the right.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a chilled glass of sweet Pedro Ximénez sherry
Present on traditional white ceramics to emphasize the colors of the Spanish flag
instructions: Bloom gelatin sheets in cold water for 5 minutes.
Combine cream, 80g diced ham, and 40ml honey in a saucepan.
Heat cream mixture until simmering. Remove from heat.
Cover saucepan. Steep ham in cream for 20 minutes.
Strain cream through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids.
Squeeze excess water from gelatin. Whisk into warm cream until dissolved.
Pour mixture into 4 molds. Refrigerate for 4 hours until set.
Preheat oven to 160°C.
Place remaining ham slices on parchment paper. Brush with remaining honey.
Bake ham for 12 minutes until crisp. Cool and break into large shards.
Cut melon into 1cm cubes. Toss with sherry vinegar.
Unmold panna cotta onto plates. Top with melon cubes and ham shards. Garnish with mint.
notes: Ensure the cream does not boil after adding gelatin to maintain a smooth set
The saltiness of the ham varies; adjust honey levels to balance the infusion
Use a very fine sieve to ensure no ham particulates remain in the panna cotta

recipes.recipe_name: Chocolate Dutch Baby
recipes.special_requests: maximize protein (without protein powder), minimize sugar
recipes.visual_description: A single wedge of a deep chocolate Dutch baby sits on a cream-colored ceramic plate. The pancake features tall, irregular, puffed edges with a porous, aerated texture. The center is slightly thinner and custardy. The color is a rich, matte dark brown from the cocoa. The plate rests on a dark oak kitchen table next to a simple silver fork and a folded linen napkin. Natural light from a nearby window highlights the craggy peaks of the crust. The background shows a hint of the seasoned cast iron skillet and a glass of milk. The arrangement is casual and home-style, emphasizing the natural textures of the baked egg batter. Every element feels authentic and warm.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while the pancake is at its maximum height
Pair with a cup of strong black coffee
Serve directly from the cast iron skillet for a rustic family presentation
instructions: Preheat oven to 220°C.
Place butter in a 25 cm cast iron skillet.
Put skillet in the oven to melt butter until bubbling.
Whisk eggs, milk, vanilla, and coffee in a large bowl.
Sift flour, cocoa powder, sugar, and baking soda into a separate bowl.
Gradually whisk dry ingredients into wet ingredients until smooth.
Remove hot skillet from oven.
Pour batter immediately into the center of the melted butter.
Bake for 18-20 minutes until the edges are high and puffed.
Do not open the oven door during the baking process.
Remove from oven and cut into 6 wedges.
notes: Use room temperature eggs and milk for the highest puff
Coffee enhances the depth of the cocoa without adding a distinct coffee flavor
The high egg content provides significant protein while the sugar is kept to a minimum

recipes.recipe_name: Paneer Makhani with Jeera Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Paneer Makhani is presented in a shallow white porcelain bowl. The paneer consists of large 3cm un-sliced cubes coated in a thick, velvety tomato-based gravy of deep ochre. A drizzle of heavy cream and finely chopped cilantro garnish the top. Adjacent to the bowl, a neat mound of Jeera Rice shows long, separate Basmati grains flecked with whole toasted cumin seeds. The setting includes a dark wooden table, a folded cotton napkin, and a pair of polished stainless steel spoons. Natural side-lighting emphasizes the glossy sauce and the fluffy texture of the rice. The arrangement is clean with ample negative space on the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm garlic naan or tandoori roti
Accompany with a side of sliced red onions and lemon wedges
Include a small bowl of mango pickle or mint chutney
instructions: Soak basmati rice in cold water for 30 minutes. Drain.
Boil rice in 800ml salted water until tender. Drain excess water.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a small pan. Sauté cumin seeds until they crackle. Fold into the cooked rice.
Puree tomatoes until smooth.
Finely dice onions.
Cut paneer into 3cm cubes.
Heat remaining oil and 25g butter in a heavy pot. Sauté onions until dark golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste. Cook for 1 minute.
Add tomato puree, chili powder, and turmeric. Simmer for 15 minutes until oil separates from the masala.
Stir in garam masala, remaining butter, and heavy cream.
Add paneer cubes to the gravy. Simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Season with salt. Garnish with chopped cilantro.
notes: Do not overcook the paneer or it will become rubbery
Kashmiri chili powder provides the signature red color without excessive heat
Ensure the rice grains are fully separate and not mushy

recipes.recipe_name: Achiote Rockfish with Sofrito Rice and Tostones
recipes.visual_description: A single, whole seared rockfish fillet sits atop a vibrant bed of sofrito-infused yellow rice. The fish features a deep reddish-orange achiote crust with charred edges. Beside the rice, three thick, circular tostones show a golden-brown, crispy exterior and a starchy, pale yellow center. The rice is fluffy and flecked with green cilantro and red peppers from the sofrito. A small wedge of lime and a sprig of fresh cilantro provide a bright green accent. The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain plate with moderate negative space. The setting includes a rustic wooden table, a small bowl of garlic dipping sauce, and a simple cotton napkin. Natural lighting highlights the textures perfectly.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with pique hot sauce
Accompany with garlic mojo dipping sauce
Provide extra lime wedges
instructions: Combine 30g achiote paste, 10g sazon, and 30ml lime juice.
Rub mixture over 4 rockfish fillets. Marinate for 15 minutes.
Heat 15ml oil in a pot. Sauté 60ml sofrito for 2 minutes.
Add 300g rice. Stir to coat in oil and sofrito.
Pour in 500ml chicken stock. Bring to boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 18 minutes.
Peel plantains. Cut into 3cm thick chunks.
Fry chunks in 180°C oil for 3 minutes. Remove and drain.
Smash chunks into flat discs using a plantain press or heavy pan.
Fry smashed discs again until crispy. Season with salt.
Heat 30ml oil in a skillet.
Sear rockfish fillets 4 minutes per side until internal temperature reaches 63°C.
Fluff rice with remaining sofrito and chopped cilantro.
Serve whole fillet over rice with tostones on the side.
notes: Use very green plantains for the crispiest tostones
Do not crowd the pan when searing the fish
Ensure rice rests for 5 minutes before fluffing

recipes.recipe_name: Cod in Acqua Pazza
recipes.visual_description: A single thick, opaque white cod fillet sits centered in a shallow white porcelain bowl. The fish is whole and unsliced. It is surrounded by a vibrant, translucent 'crazy water' broth made of golden extra virgin olive oil and light red tomato juices. Halved cherry tomatoes are scattered around the fish, their skins slightly wrinkled from gentle poaching. Thin translucent slices of garlic and bright green chopped parsley float in the shimmering liquid. The broth is fluid and glossy. The dish is presented on a clean wooden bistro table with a white cotton napkin. A side of thick-cut toasted sourdough bread rests on a small plate. Natural side lighting emphasizes the moist flakes of the fish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with toasted crusty bread to soak up the poaching liquid
Pair with a chilled dry Italian white wine like Vermentino
Present in shallow wide bowls to showcase the broth
instructions: Season cod fillets with salt and pepper.
Slice garlic cloves into thin slivers.
Halve all cherry tomatoes.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add garlic and chili flakes to the oil.
Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add halved tomatoes to the skillet.
Cook for 3 minutes until tomatoes soften slightly.
Pour in white wine and simmer for 2 minutes.
Add water and bring to a gentle simmer.
Place cod fillets into the liquid in a single layer.
Cover the skillet with a lid.
Poach fish for 7 minutes until the internal texture is opaque.
Remove the lid.
Drizzle remaining 30ml olive oil into the broth.
Swirl the pan gently to create a light emulsion.
Stir in chopped parsley.
Transfer fish and broth to shallow bowls immediately.
notes: Use high-quality extra virgin olive oil for the final emulsion
Do not let the liquid boil vigorously or the fish will toughen
Ensure the cod is fresh for the best flake texture

recipes.recipe_name: Sweet Onion Ice Cream with Lemon Gel and Black Sesame Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfect quenelle of ivory sweet onion ice cream sits off-center on a large, matte white bone china plate. To the left, vibrant translucent lemon gel is piped in precise, varying-sized spheres. A textured mound of jet-black sesame crumble serves as an organic base for the ice cream. Thin, architectural shards of white sesame tuile are tucked vertically into the quenelle for height. Fine julienne strips of candied lemon zest are scattered with artistic intent across the composition. The arrangement flows naturally across the plate with significant negative space. The setting is a grey-veined white marble surface under dramatic professional lighting, featuring a polished silver dessert spoon and a crisp white linen napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a palate-cleansing final course in a multi-course tasting menu
Pair with a chilled Sauternes or a late-harvest Riesling
Present on chilled bone china to maintain the ice cream texture
instructions: Roast diced onions at 160°C for 45 minutes until soft and sweet.
Simmer cream, milk, and roasted onions in a saucepan for 10 minutes.
Strain mixture through a fine-mesh sieve and discard onion solids.
Whisk egg yolks with 100g sugar until pale.
Temper hot onion-cream into yolks and return to heat.
Cook to 82°C while stirring constantly.
Chill custard completely and churn in an ice cream machine.
Boil lemon juice, remaining sugar, and agar-agar for 1 minute.
Set in refrigerator until firm, then blend into a smooth gel.
Pulse black sesame seeds, butter, flour, and a pinch of sugar into crumbs.
Bake crumble at 170°C for 12 minutes and cool.
Blanch lemon zest three times in boiling water, then simmer in sugar syrup.
notes: Ensure onions do not brown during roasting to maintain a clean ivory color
The onion flavor should be subtle and reminiscent of sweet corn
Blend the lemon gel at high speed for a perfectly glass-like finish

recipes.recipe_name: Sweet Milk-Poached Herring with Pickled Cucumber Compote
recipes.visual_description: A single portion served on a rustic white ceramic plate with a slight lip. The center features two whole, skin-on herring fillets, poached until opaque and glistening. A thick, ivory-colored sweet milk sauce pools around the base of the fish. To the side, a mound of finely diced pickled cucumbers, translucent and bright green, provides a sharp color contrast.
