Provide a side of Prik Nam Pla (fish sauce with chilies)
Eat using a large spoon in the right hand and a fork in the left to push food onto the spoon
instructions: Clean agati flowers and remove the bitter yellow stamens from the center.
Heat vegetable oil in a large deep pan over medium heat.
Fry red curry paste for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add 150ml of coconut milk and stir until the oil separates from the cream.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk and stock. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Stir in fish sauce and palm sugar until dissolved.
Add torn kaffir lime leaves.
Place the whole sea bass fillets into the simmering liquid.
Poach fish for 6 minutes until opaque and cooked through.
Submerge the agati flowers in the curry. Cook for 60 seconds until wilted.
Remove from heat immediately to preserve flower color.
notes: Ensure the stamens are removed from the agati flowers to prevent excessive bitterness.
Do not overcook the flowers; they should retain their shape.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Bell Pepper Consommé with Confit Onion Petals
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, ruby-red bell pepper consommé fills the base of a wide, shallow bone china bowl. Three translucent, ivory-colored confit onion petals are positioned organically in the center. Precise 5mm cubes of roasted red bell pepper are tucked inside the petals. A single drop of emerald-green herb oil creates a sharp contrast on the liquid surface. The bowl sits on a grey-veined white Carrara marble surface. Side-lighting creates soft shadows, emphasizing the liquid's clarity. The composition is minimalist with significant negative space around the central elements. A polished silver spoon rests on a precisely folded white linen napkin. The presentation is sophisticated, following modern French fine-dining aesthetics.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a light opening course in a multi-course tasting menu
Pour the hot consommé tableside from a small porcelain pitcher
Accompany with a chilled glass of dry Sancerre
instructions: Char 800g red peppers over an open flame until skin blackens.
Place peppers in a bowl. Cover with plastic wrap for 10 minutes.
Peel, deseed, and rinse the peppers.
Reserve 200g of roasted peppers. Cut into 5mm cubes.
Blend remaining 600g peppers with 500ml vegetable stock.
Strain liquid through a fine chinois.
Whisk 2 egg whites into the cold liquid.
Heat liquid slowly to a simmer. Allow the egg white raft to form.
Strain liquid through a muslin cloth to obtain a clear consommé.
Season consommé with 10ml sherry vinegar and salt.
Peel 300g onions. Separate into individual petals.
Submerge petals in 100ml olive oil with thyme.
Cook at 90°C for 40 minutes until translucent.
Place 3 confit onion petals and pepper cubes in a shallow bowl.
Pour hot consommé over ingredients. Garnish with micro-basil.
notes: Maintain the oil temperature at exactly 90°C to ensure onions remain translucent and do not brown.
Ensure the consommé is completely cold before adding egg whites for effective clarification.
Use a high-quality sherry vinegar to balance the sweetness of the roasted peppers.

recipes.recipe_name: Ginger Beer Glazed Pork Belly
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Ginger Beer Glazed Pork Belly presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl. Three 5cm square chunks of pork belly are the focal point, glistening with a dark, sticky amber glaze. The meat is tender and intact, not sliced. Two vibrant green bok choy halves, blanched to a crisp-tender texture, lean against the pork. The base is a neat mound of steamed white jasmine rice. A glossy reduction of ginger beer and soy pools at the base of the meat. Garnished with 3cm spring onion batons and fine julienne ginger. The setting is a modern bistro table with dark wood grain, a grey linen napkin, and a pair of dark wood chopsticks.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of quick-pickled cucumbers
Provide high-quality wooden chopsticks
Accompanied by a small bowl of extra glaze

ingredients.name: Baby bok choy, halved and steamed

instructions: Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Sear pork belly chunks until browned on all sides.
Drain and discard excess fat from the pot.
Add ginger slices, crushed garlic, star anise, and cinnamon.
Cook 1 minute until aromatic.
Pour in ginger beer, light soy sauce, and dark soy sauce.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Simmer covered for 90 minutes until meat is tender.
Remove pork chunks and set aside.
Boil the cooking liquid on high heat until reduced to a thick, syrupy glaze.
Return pork to the pot and toss to coat thoroughly.
Serve pork chunks over steamed jasmine rice with bok choy.
notes: Use a high-quality, spicy ginger beer for a deeper flavor profile
Ensure the glaze is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon before returning the pork

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Spiced Bananas with Cocoa Cream
recipes.visual_description: Golden-brown fried banana rounds, cut into thick 2cm cylinders, are piled naturally in a shallow, matte ceramic bowl. The bananas show a caramelized, slightly crispy exterior with visible grains of coarse sea salt and ground cumin. A small, rustic terracotta ramekin sits next to the bowl, filled with a glossy, dark chocolate and cream sauce. The sauce has a deep mahogany color and is dusted lightly with red chili powder. The entire dish is presented on a well-used dark wooden table with a simple, folded cloth napkin. The lighting is warm and domestic, emphasizing the soft textures of the fruit and the liquid sheen of the savory cocoa dip. The arrangement is unpretentious and ready for sharing.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a mid-afternoon snack (merienda)
Present on a communal wooden board for family sharing
Pair with a strong, unsweetened coffee
instructions: Peel bananas and cut into thick 2cm rounds.
Heat butter and oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Place banana rounds in the skillet in a single layer.
Fry bananas for 3 minutes per side until golden brown and caramelized.
Transfer bananas to a plate lined with paper towels to drain.
Sprinkle warm bananas immediately with sea salt and ground cumin.
Heat heavy cream in a small saucepan over medium heat until simmering.
Remove from heat and add finely chopped dark chocolate and chili powder.
Whisk cream and chocolate until smooth and glossy.
Serve the warm savory bananas on a platter with the cocoa cream in a side bowl for dipping.
notes: Ensure bananas are firm to prevent them from becoming mushy when fried
Adjust chili powder quantity to reach desired heat level
The dark chocolate must be at least 70% cocoa to maintain the savory profile

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish-Style Paprika Chicken Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish chicken rice is presented on a clean white porcelain plate. The base consists of a generous mound of moist, orange-hued rice mixed with small cubes of soft red bell pepper and bright green peas. A whole, golden-brown seared chicken thigh sits prominently on top of the rice, showing a crisp, seasoned skin. The meat is not sliced. A fresh lemon wedge is placed on the side of the plate. Finely chopped green parsley is scattered over the dish for contrast. The setting features a modern bistro wooden table with a folded cotton napkin and a traditional stainless steel fork. Natural lighting emphasizes the textures of the crispy skin and fluffy rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a traditional terracotta cazuela for communal dining
Accompany with a side of garlic aioli
Provide fresh crusty bread to soak up juices
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and 5g of paprika.
Heat oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until crispy.
Flip chicken and sear for 4 minutes. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion and red pepper to the same pan. Sauté for 5 minutes.
Stir in garlic, remaining paprika, and ketchup. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add rice to the pan. Stir to coat grains in the base.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a boil.
Place chicken thighs back into the rice skin-side up.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 18 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Stir in peas. Cover and rest for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Ketchup provides a balanced sweet and acidic base for the rice similar to traditional tomato frito.
Ensure the rice is not stirred after adding the stock to develop a crust at the bottom.

recipes.recipe_name: Grilled Chicken with Tomato and Cucumber Horiatiki
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean grilled chicken served over a vibrant salad on a clean white porcelain plate. The hero ingredients are the large 2cm tomato wedges and 1.5cm thick cucumber half-moons, tossed in a glistening herb-flecked vinaigrette. The chicken is presented as charred, golden-brown 3cm chunks, never sliced, piled naturally atop the vegetables. Thin red onion rounds and whole dark Kalamata olives add visual depth. A block of creamy white feta is roughly crumbled over the dish. The setting is a rustic wooden bistro table with a linen napkin and a side of warm, charred pita bread. Natural side-lighting emphasizes the textures of the seared meat and juicy, fresh vegetables.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm pita bread
Accompany with a side of tzatziki
Provide extra lemon wedges for acidity
instructions: Cut chicken into 3cm chunks.
Whisk 40ml olive oil, 20ml lemon juice, and 5g oregano in a bowl.
Marinate chicken in mixture for 30 minutes.
Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
Grill chicken chunks until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Cut tomatoes into 2cm wedges.
Peel cucumbers partially and slice into 1.5cm thick half-moons.
Slice red onion into thin rounds.
Whisk remaining oil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Toss tomatoes, cucumbers, onions, and olives with the dressing.
Place salad on individual plates.
Top with grilled chicken chunks.
Crumble feta cheese over the top.
Garnish with remaining oregano.
notes: Use high-quality Greek olive oil for authentic flavor.
Do not overmix the salad to keep the tomato wedges intact.

recipes.recipe_name: Beer-Battered Fish Tacos with Cucumber-Tomato Salsa
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of three corn tortillas rests on a clean white porcelain plate. Each tortilla contains two thick, whole chunks of beer-battered cod, fried to a deep golden-brown with a visible crispy texture. The fish sits atop a bed of finely shredded, vibrant green romaine lettuce. A salsa composed of small-diced red tomatoes and peeled, diced green cucumbers is spooned over the fish. A dollop of smooth, white sour cream finishes each taco. The plate is set on a dark wood table with a folded white cotton napkin. A lime wedge sits on the side. Natural light emphasizes the crunch of the batter and the freshness of the vegetables.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of pickled jalapeños
Accompany with a cold Mexican lager
Present on a traditional hand-painted ceramic platter for family-style sharing
instructions: Cut fish into 5 cm thick chunks.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and 5 g salt in a bowl.
Whisk beer into flour mixture until smooth. Let batter rest 15 minutes.
Dice tomatoes and cucumber into 5 mm cubes. Mix with 15 ml lime juice and chopped cilantro.
Mix sour cream with remaining lime juice and a pinch of salt.
Shred lettuce into very thin strips.
Heat oil to 180°C in a heavy pot.
Pat fish chunks dry. Dip into batter to coat fully.
Fry fish chunks in batches for 4 minutes until golden and crispy.
Drain fish on a wire rack.
Warm tortillas in a dry skillet for 30 seconds per side.
Place lettuce on tortillas. Add two fish chunks per taco. Top with salsa and a dollop of sour cream.
notes: Ensure the beer is very cold for a crispier batter
Maintain oil temperature at 180°C to prevent greasy fish
Pat the fish extremely dry before dipping in batter to ensure it sticks

recipes.recipe_name: Acai and Coconut Brigadeiros
recipes.visual_description: Nine uniform, sphere-shaped acai brigadeiros are arranged casually on a rustic, off-white ceramic platter with natural imperfections. Each sweet is approximately 2cm in diameter. The deep, dark purple acai-infused centers are completely coated in fine, snowy-white desiccated coconut, providing a high-contrast texture. One brigadeiro is sliced in half to reveal the dense, fudgy, and glossy purple interior. The platter sits on a distressed dark wood table in a sunlit kitchen. Beside the platter lies a simple, folded linen napkin and a small cup of dark Brazilian coffee. The lighting is warm and natural, highlighting the crystalline texture of the coconut and the rich, authentic color of the acai.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a strong Brazilian cafezinho (espresso-style coffee)
Present in colorful paper liners (forminhas) for a festive touch
Enjoy as a mid-afternoon treat or party snack
instructions: Place acai pulp in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Simmer until the volume reduces by half.
Add the condensed milk and butter to the reduced acai.
Cook over medium-low heat while stirring constantly with a silicone spatula.
Continue stirring until the mixture thickens and pulls away completely from the bottom of the pan.
Pour the mixture onto a lightly buttered plate.
Allow to cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Grease your palms with a small amount of butter.
Scoop small portions and roll into uniform 2cm spheres.
Roll each sphere in desiccated coconut until fully coated.
Place each sweet into a small paper candy liner.
notes: Ensure you reduce the acai pulp first to prevent the mixture from becoming too runny.
Stir constantly to prevent the condensed milk from burning on the bottom.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Lentil and Mushroom Ragù
recipes.visual_description: A deep white porcelain bowl holds a single portion of thick, savory lentil and mushroom ragù. The ragù features earthy brown lentils, 2cm chunks of textured soy protein, and quartered button mushrooms coated in a rich, dark tomato and white wine sauce. Nestled alongside the ragù are 3cm cubes of golden-brown roasted potatoes, showing visible flecks of dried rosemary. Small 1cm dice of vibrant green zucchini are interspersed throughout the stew. The dish is finished with thin shavings of pale parmesan cheese and three whole, bright green basil leaves placed off-center. The composition is balanced with clean margins. Natural side lighting highlights the glossy sauce and the crisp texture of the potato skins.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty sourdough bread
Pair with a crisp dry white wine
Present in individual ceramic crocks for a rustic feel
instructions: Soak textured soy protein in warm water for 15 minutes. Drain and squeeze dry.
Toss potato cubes with 15ml olive oil, rosemary, salt, and pepper.
Roast potatoes at 200°C for 25 minutes until golden and crisp.
Heat remaining olive oil in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Sauté onion, celery, and mushrooms until vegetables soften and brown.
Add garlic, soy protein chunks, and zucchini. Cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste, cumin, and paprika. Toast for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Scrape the bottom of the pot to deglaze.
Add lentils, bay leaf, thyme, and vegetable stock. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 30 minutes until lentils are tender.
Remove bay leaf. Stir in lemon juice, salt, pepper, and cayenne.
Place roasted potatoes in a shallow bowl. Spoon ragù over the top.
Garnish with shaved parmesan and fresh basil.
notes: Ensure textured soy protein is squeezed very dry to allow it to absorb the ragù flavors
Add more stock if the ragù becomes too thick during simmering
Use high-quality parmesan for the best salty finish

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Beef and Apple Mincemeat Tart
recipes.visual_description: A single tartlet sits on a white porcelain plate atop a dark wooden table. The golden-brown shortcrust pastry shell has a crisp, fluted edge. Inside, the filling features 5mm cubes of tender beef and translucent, softened apple chunks coated in a dark, glossy amber glaze. Fine specks of cracked black pepper are visible throughout the rich mixture. The arrangement is clean and focused, showing the internal texture of the syrupy mincemeat. A small, fresh bay leaf is placed neatly on the plate rim for color. Natural side-lighting emphasizes the flaky texture of the crust and the moist sheen of the fruit and meat filling. A silver dessert fork rests on a white linen napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm with a dollop of clotted cream
Pair with a glass of fortified dessert wine
Traditional festive season dessert presentation

ingredients.name: Beef chuck, finely diced into 5mm cubes
Granny Smith apples, peeled and diced

instructions: Melt butter in a heavy-bottomed saucepan over medium heat.
Sauté minced onion until soft and translucent.
Add beef cubes to the pan. Brown for 4 minutes.
Stir in diced apples, brown sugar, black pepper, and salt.
Add bay leaves and water to the mixture.
Simmer on low heat for 40 minutes until liquid reduces to a thick syrup.
Remove bay leaves. Allow filling to cool completely.
Preheat oven to 180°C.
Line four 10cm tart tins with shortcrust pastry.
Fill pastry shells with the cooled beef and apple mixture.
Bake for 25 minutes until the pastry edges are golden-brown.
Remove from oven and let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Ensure beef is diced very small to integrate with the fruit texture.
Cooling the filling is essential to prevent a soggy pastry base.
The bay leaf provides a subtle herbal depth that balances the sugar.

recipes.recipe_name: Cantonese Black Pepper Beef and Potato
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Cantonese Black Pepper Beef and Potato presented on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish consists of 2cm cubes of seared beef, deeply browned and coated in a dark, glossy black pepper sauce. These are mixed with 2cm cubes of potatoes featuring a crispy, golden-brown exterior. The ingredients are arranged in a natural, centered pile with visible negative space. Bright green 3cm scallion batons provide a fresh color contrast against the dark glaze. The setting is a modern bistro with a dark wood table. A pair of dark wood chopsticks sits on a ceramic rest. Natural lighting emphasizes the textures of the succulent meat and crisp potatoes.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice
Accompany with a side of lightly blanched bok choy
Provide a small dish of chili oil for dipping
instructions: Cut beef into 2cm cubes.
Mix beef with soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, cornstarch, and half the black pepper.
Marinate for 20 minutes.
Peel potatoes and cut into 2cm cubes.
Parboil potato cubes in salted water for 5 minutes.
Drain potatoes and pat thoroughly dry.
Heat 30ml oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Fry potato cubes until golden and crispy on all sides. Remove and set aside.
Heat remaining oil in the wok over high heat.
Sear beef cubes in a single layer until browned. Remove and set aside.
Add garlic and ginger to the wok. Stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Return beef and potatoes to the wok.
Add oyster sauce, sugar, and remaining black pepper.
Toss over high heat for 1 minute to glaze.
Add scallion batons. Toss once and serve.
notes: Ensure the wok is smoking hot before adding beef to achieve wok hei flavor
Patting the potatoes dry is essential for a crispy exterior
Do not overcook the beef to maintain a tender interior

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Beef and Apple Mincemeat Tart

recipes.recipe_name: Stir-Fried Napa Cabbage with Pork Belly and Fried Dough Twists
recipes.visual_description: A shallow, wide celadon ceramic bowl holds a vibrant heap of stir-fried elements. The hero ingredient, Napa cabbage, shows a mix of translucent, ivory-white stems and wilted, emerald-green leaves, both glistening with a savory soy glaze. Interspersed are golden-brown, irregular chunks of fried dough twists, their textured surfaces partially softened by the sauce. Thick 3cm squares of seared pork belly provide a rich, caramelized contrast. Purple onion wedges are softened but retain their shape. The dish is garnished with a scatter of fresh scallion rounds. The setting includes a pair of dark wood chopsticks on a rest, a small side dish of pickled garlic, and a clean linen napkin placed on a light oak table.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed white rice
Accompany with Laba garlic (vinegar-pickled garlic)
Pair with a light jasmine tea
instructions: Slice pork belly into 3cm squares, approximately 5mm thick.
Tear napa cabbage leaves into 5cm pieces, separating white stems from green leaves.
Slice red onion into 1cm wedges.
Break fried dough twists into 4cm irregular chunks.
Mince garlic and ginger finely.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Add pork belly squares. Render fat until meat is golden and edges are crisp.
Add onion wedges, garlic, ginger, and dried chilies. Stir-fry for 1 minute.
Increase heat to high. Add cabbage stems. Stir-fry for 2 minutes until slightly softened.
Add cabbage leaves. Stir-fry until just wilted.
Whisk light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, vinegar, and sugar in a small bowl.
Pour sauce over the vegetables.
Add fried dough twist chunks. Toss rapidly for 30 seconds to coat in sauce.
Garnish with sliced scallion rounds and serve immediately.
notes: Add the fried dough twists at the very end to maintain a slight crunch.
The dark soy sauce is primarily for a deep amber color.
High heat is essential for wok hei flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Stir-Fried Napa Cabbage with Pork Belly and Fried Dough Twists
recipes.visual_description: A shallow, wide celadon ceramic bowl holds a vibrant heap of stir-fried elements. The hero ingredient, Napa cabbage, shows a mix of translucent, ivory-white stems and wilted, emerald-green leaves, both glistening with a savory soy glaze. Interspersed are golden-brown, irregular chunks of fried dough twists, their textured surfaces partially softened by the sauce. Thick 3cm squares of seared pork belly provide a rich, caramelized contrast. Purple onion wedges are softened but retain their shape. The dish is garnished with a scatter of fresh scallion rounds. The setting includes a pair of dark wood chopsticks on a rest, a small side dish of pickled garlic, and a clean linen napkin placed on a light oak table.

Accompany with Laba garlic (vinegar-pickled garlic)

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Peach and Grape Salad with Crispy Poached Eggs
recipes.visual_description: The entire white porcelain plate is visible, showcasing a balanced Mediterranean composition with ample negative space. A bed of fresh arugula supports thick, roasted peach wedges and halved red grapes. The peaches show dark charred edges from roasting. The grapes are slightly blistered and juicy. A single, whole crispy poached egg sits as the focal point, featuring a golden-brown panko crust. Small, irregular crumbles of white goat cheese are scattered naturally. A thin stream of dark balsamic dressing accents the plate. The scene is set on a light oak table with a white cotton napkin and polished silver fork. Natural light emphasizes the textures of the crispy egg and soft fruit.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm toasted sourdough bread
Pair with a chilled dry Vermentino or Sauvignon Blanc
Present as a sophisticated bistro-style lunch
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut peaches into thick wedges.
Halve the red grapes.
Toss peach wedges and grapes with 20ml oil, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Roast fruit for 12 minutes until caramelized.
Poach 4 eggs in simmering water for 3 minutes.
Transfer poached eggs to an ice bath and dry carefully.
Beat remaining 2 eggs in a bowl.
Dredge poached eggs in flour, then beaten egg, then panko.
Fry breaded eggs in oil at 180°C until golden brown.
Whisk remaining oil and balsamic vinegar together.
Place arugula on four plates.
Arrange roasted peach wedges and grape halves over greens.
Place one whole crispy egg in the center of each plate.
Top with crumbled goat cheese and dressing.
notes: Use firm peaches to prevent them from turning mushy during roasting
Maintain the oil temperature at 180°C for the egg to ensure a crisp exterior without overcooking the yolk
Dry the poached eggs thoroughly before breading to ensure the coating adheres

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Hungarian Cottage Cheese Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Savory Hungarian Cottage Cheese Pasta is presented on a wide white porcelain plate. The hand-torn noodles are irregularly shaped 3cm squares, coated in a glossy, ivory-colored sauce made from cottage cheese and milk. The dish is topped with 1cm cubes of deep-golden, crispy smoked bacon and dollops of thick, cool sour cream. Freshly crumbled cottage cheese provides a pebbled texture across the surface. The arrangement is natural and flowing, emphasizing the rustic origins with a refined finish. The plate sits on a textured wooden bistro table with a folded cotton napkin and a polished fork. Soft side-lighting captures the steam and the contrast between the matte cheese and glistening bacon.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with pickled Hungarian wax peppers.
Pair with a chilled cucumber salad.
Eat as a traditional heavy main course.
instructions: Mix 400g flour and 4 eggs.
Knead dough until firm and smooth.
Roll dough to 2mm thickness.
Tear into 3cm irregular squares.
Boil in salted water 4 minutes.
Dice 150g smoked bacon into 1cm cubes.
Sauté bacon until cubes are crisp.
Drain noodles.
Toss noodles in 30ml rendered bacon fat.
Whisk 500g cottage cheese with 60ml milk.
Fold cheese and 125ml sour cream into noodles.
Heat over low flame for 2 minutes.
Top with 125ml sour cream and bacon.
notes: Use high-fat cottage cheese for a richer flavor.
Drain the pasta thoroughly to prevent a watery sauce.
Ensure the bacon cubes are very crispy for texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Potato Gnocchi with Brown Butter and Sage
recipes.visual_description: The dish features hand-formed potato gnocchi, cut into uniform 2cm batons, presented in a clean white porcelain shallow bowl. The gnocchi have a soft, pillowy texture with a light golden sheen from the brown butter. Dark green, crispy sage leaves are scattered naturally over the gnocchi. A delicate dusting of finely grated Parmigiano-Reggiano covers the center of the arrangement. The gnocchi are placed in an organic, free-flowing pile, leaving clear negative space around the rim of the bowl. The setting is a light wood bistro table with a neutral linen napkin and a single silver fork. Natural, soft light emphasizes the matte texture of the cheese and the glossy butter sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in warmed shallow bowls
Pair with a crisp dry white wine such as Gavi or Pinot Grigio
Provide extra Parmigiano-Reggiano at the table
instructions: Boil whole unpeeled potatoes in salted water for 25 minutes until tender.
Drain and peel potatoes while still warm.
Pass potatoes through a ricer onto a clean work surface.
Allow potato steam to evaporate for 5 minutes.
Create a well in the potatoes and add flour, beaten egg, and salt.
Mix by hand until a soft dough forms. Do not overwork.
Divide dough into four portions.
Roll each portion into a rope 2cm thick.
Cut ropes into 2cm batons using a bench scraper.
Boil gnocchi in salted water. Remove with a slotted spoon once they float.
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat until it foams and turns light brown.
Add sage leaves and fry for 1 minute until crisp.
Transfer gnocchi to the skillet. Toss gently to coat in brown butter.
Season with black pepper and serve immediately with grated cheese.
notes: Peeling potatoes while hot ensures a lighter texture.
Avoid over-mixing the dough to prevent the gnocchi from becoming gummy.
Ensure the butter reaches a nutty aroma before adding the sage.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Pearl Mushroom Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy pearl mushroom soup fills a wide, shallow ceramic bowl. The bowl features a rustic, hand-thrown texture with a matte grey finish. The soup is a deep, earthy beige with a thick, velvety consistency. Five whole, deeply browned pearl mushrooms are nestled together in the center. A drizzle of heavy cream forms a delicate white swirl across the surface. Tiny, fresh green thyme leaves are sprinkled over the mushrooms. The bowl sits on a heavy, dark oak table. A rustic crusty bread roll sits on a small side plate. Warm, natural light enters from the side, casting soft shadows and highlighting the glossy texture of the whole mushrooms.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Warm crusty baguette
Salted French butter
Dry white wine
instructions: Wipe mushrooms clean with a damp cloth.
Slice half the mushrooms into thick pieces.
Leave the remaining mushrooms whole.
Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion and sauté until translucent.
Add garlic and thyme. Cook for 1 minute.
Increase heat and add all mushrooms.
Sauté until mushrooms are golden brown.
Remove 12 whole mushrooms and set aside for garnish.
Pour in vegetable stock.
Simmer for 15 minutes.
Blend half the soup in a blender until smooth.
Return the blended soup to the pot.
Stir in heavy cream and heat through.
Season with salt and pepper.
Ladle into bowls.
Top each bowl with reserved whole mushrooms.
notes: Do not boil the soup after adding the cream to prevent curdling.
Use a mix of white and brown pearl mushrooms for deeper flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Whipped Cottage Cheese and Poached Egg on Fried Sourdough
recipes.visual_description: A single thick slice of golden-brown fried sourdough sits centered on a matte white porcelain plate. The bread is topped with a thick, velvety layer of whipped white cottage cheese. A single, perfectly translucent whole poached egg rests centrally atop the cheese, its surface smooth and white. Vibrant green finely chopped chives are scattered over the egg and cheese. Four thin, crisp radish circles are placed naturally around the egg. A light drizzle of golden olive oil circles the bread. The scene is set on a dark wood table with a folded grey linen napkin and a silver fork. Natural side lighting highlights the textures of the crispy bread and creamy cheese.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of lightly dressed bitter greens
Accompany with a glass of dry sparkling water or white wine
instructions: Process cottage cheese in a blender with lemon zest and salt until smooth.
Heat butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Fry sourdough slices until golden and crisp on both sides.
Bring water and vinegar to a gentle simmer in a deep saucepan.
Crack eggs into the water and poach for 3 minutes until whites are set.
Remove eggs with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Spread whipped cottage cheese thickly over each slice of fried bread.
Place one whole poached egg on top of the cheese layer.
Top with finely chopped chives and thinly sliced radish rounds.
Drizzle with olive oil and season with black pepper.
notes: Ensure the cottage cheese is at room temperature before blending for a smoother texture
Use high-quality sourdough for the best structural integrity after frying

recipes.recipe_name: Potatoes Lyonnaise
recipes.visual_description: The dish features golden-brown, crispy potato rounds piled naturally on a clean white porcelain plate. Deeply caramelized onions and translucent minced garlic are interspersed throughout the potatoes, adding rich mahogany highlights. The potatoes are cut into uniform 5mm discs, showing a mix of tender centers and crunchy, seared edges. A light sprinkle of finely chopped flat-leaf parsley provides a vibrant green contrast against the warm amber and gold tones of the vegetables. The plate is set on a dark oak bistro table. Beside the plate lies a folded white cotton napkin and a polished silver fork. Natural side-lighting highlights the glistening texture of the butter-sautéed surfaces. The arrangement is organic and centered, with moderate negative space around the plate's edge.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a warm ceramic dish
Pair with roasted chicken or steak
Serve alongside a simple green salad with vinaigrette
instructions: Peel potatoes.
Slice into 5mm rounds.
Boil potatoes in salted water for 5 minutes.
Drain and pat dry.
Peel and thinly slice onions.
Mince garlic.
Melt 20g butter with 10ml oil in a large pan.
Add onions.
Cook on medium-low until dark golden brown.
Add garlic.
Cook 1 minute.
Remove onion mixture from pan.
Heat remaining oil and butter in the same pan.
Add potatoes in a single layer.
Fry until golden and crisp on both sides.
Return onions and garlic to the pan.
Toss gently to combine.
Deglaze with vinegar.
Season with salt and pepper.
Garnish with chopped parsley.
notes: Use waxy potatoes to ensure the slices maintain their shape during frying
Caramelize onions slowly to develop deep sweetness without burning

recipes.recipe_name: Mor Kuzhambu with Toor Dal Vadai
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a deep white porcelain bowl. The Mor Kuzhambu features a pale, creamy yellow color with a smooth, fluid consistency. Three golden-brown, textured toor dal vadai, shaped as small thick rounds, are placed in the center. The surface is drizzled with a vibrant tempering of glossy black mustard seeds, toasted red chilies, and crisp dark green curry leaves. Fresh green cilantro leaves are scattered on top. The bowl sits on a rustic wooden surface next to fluffy steamed rice. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the contrast between the velvety yogurt sauce and the crispy fritters. Moderate negative space surrounds the bowl. The entire plate is visible.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed Ponni or Basmati rice.
Accompany with crispy appalam (lentil crackers).
Provide a side of spicy mango or lime pickle.
instructions: Soak 150g toor dal in water for 2 hours.
Soak 50g toor dal separately for 30 minutes.
Drain 150g dal thoroughly. Grind with 1 chili and salt into a coarse paste.
Shape dal paste into small, thick 3cm rounds.
Heat oil to 180°C in a deep pan.
Fry dal rounds until golden and crisp. Drain on paper towels.
Grind 50g soaked dal, coconut, ginger, cumin, and 3 chilies with 50ml water to a fine paste.
Whisk curd with turmeric and salt in a heavy-bottomed pot.
Stir the coconut-dal paste into the whisked curd.
Heat the mixture over low flame. Stir constantly until it begins to steam.
Do not allow the curd mixture to boil or it will split.
Add the fried dal rounds to the warm curry.
Heat 15ml oil in a small tempering pan.
Add mustard seeds, red chilies, curry leaves, and asafoetida.
Pour the hot tempering over the curry and garnish with cilantro.
notes: Always whisk the curd until smooth before heating to prevent lumps.
The small amount of soaked dal ground into the base provides body and prevents separation.
Add the vadai just before serving to maintain their texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Vietnamese Braised Chicken with Radish and Carrots
recipes.visual_description: A shallow ceramic bowl holds glossy, dark amber-colored chicken chunks and tender root vegetables. The chicken is cut into large, irregular 5cm pieces, showing a rich caramelized glaze. Interspersed are soft, translucent 3cm cubes of daikon radish and vibrant 2cm thick carrot rounds, both softened from braising. A thin, savory reduction pools at the base. Fresh green coriander sprigs are scattered over the top for contrast. The dish sits on a dark wood table next to a small porcelain bowl of steamed white rice and bamboo chopsticks. Natural side lighting highlights the succulent texture of the meat and the sheen of the sauce. The arrangement is organic and uncrowded.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice
Provide a side of fresh cucumber slices
Accompany with a small dish of chili-infused fish sauce
instructions: Cut chicken into 5cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Peel radish and carrots. Cut radish into 3cm cubes. Cut carrots into 2cm rounds.
Heat oil and sugar in a heavy pot over medium heat. Stir until sugar melts into a dark amber caramel.
Add chicken chunks to the pot. Sear until browned and coated in caramel.
Add minced garlic. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in fish sauce and water. Bring to a boil.
Add radish and carrot pieces to the liquid.
Lower heat. Cover and simmer for 25 minutes.
Remove lid. Simmer for 10 minutes until sauce reduces and chicken reaches 75°C.
Garnish with chopped coriander before serving.
notes: Do not let the sugar burn past dark amber or it will become bitter
Ensure chicken chunks are uniform for even cooking
The radish will absorb the savory-sweet braising liquid as it cools

recipes.recipe_name: Dahi Chicken Curry
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a shallow white porcelain bowl, centered on a light oak bistro table. Large 4cm chunks of succulent chicken are coated in a thick, velvety yogurt-based sauce with a vibrant ochre hue. The sauce shows visible specks of toasted cumin and finely diced caramelized onions. A generous garnish of fresh, bright green cilantro leaves is scattered over the top. Beside the bowl lies a folded piece of charred, buttery naan and a small mound of fluffy, long-grain basmati rice. A single cotton napkin sits to the left. The lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the creamy texture of the gravy and the charred edges of the bread. The composition emphasizes the rich sauce and the intact, tender meat pieces.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm buttered naan or garlic roti
Accompany with long-grain basmati rice
Provide a side of sliced red onions and lemon wedges

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs, boneless, cut into 4cm chunks

instructions: Whisk yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, chili powder, and salt in a large bowl.
Add chicken chunks to the yogurt mixture and coat thoroughly.
Marinate for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat.
Add cumin seeds and toast until they sizzle.
Add finely diced onions and sauté until deep golden brown.
Add marinated chicken and all remaining marinade to the pan.
Reduce heat to low and cover with a lid.
Simmer for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Stir in garam masala and remove from heat.
Garnish with fresh cilantro before serving.
notes: Do not cook on high heat after adding yogurt to prevent curdling
Use full-fat Greek yogurt for the creamiest consistency
Kashmiri chili powder provides color without excessive heat

recipes.recipe_name: Potato and White Chocolate Entremet with Salted Caramel
recipes.visual_description: A single vertical slice of a circular entremet is positioned on a pristine white porcelain plate with a thin gold rim. The internal structure shows a golden potato-almond sponge base, a fluid salted caramel center, and a dense, pale ivory potato-white chocolate mousse. The cake is encased in a perfectly smooth, translucent mirror glaze that reflects the light. A single, translucent potato tuille, fried until golden and crisp, is placed as an architectural garnish on the top surface. The plate is set on a white marble display with significant negative space. Lighting is sharp and professional, creating soft shadows. The presentation is minimalist and refined, showcasing the clean layers and technical precision of the pastry work.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve on chilled fine porcelain
Pair with a glass of Sauternes or late-harvest Riesling
Use a silver dessert fork for service
instructions: Peel and boil 300g potatoes in unsalted water until very soft.
Pass hot potatoes through a fine-mesh tamis to create a smooth puree.
Whisk 100g potato puree with almond flour, 2 eggs, 50g sugar, and 30ml oil.
Spread mixture 1cm thick on a silicone mat.
Bake at 170°C for 12 minutes until set.
Cut into 8cm diameter circles once cooled.
Caramelize 100g sugar in a saucepan to a deep amber color.
Deglaze with 50ml warm cream and 2g sea salt.
Pour into 6cm disc molds and freeze until solid.
Soak gelatin leaves in ice water for 5 minutes.
Melt white chocolate with 100ml cream over a double boiler.
Whisk in squeezed gelatin and 100g potato puree until emulsified.
Fold in 200ml softly whipped cream gently.
Fill 10cm spherical silicone molds halfway with mousse.
Insert frozen caramel disc and potato sponge circle.
Top with remaining mousse and freeze for 6 hours.
Peel remaining potato into paper-thin slices.
Fry slices in remaining oil at 150°C until translucent and crisp.
Unmold frozen entremet and coat with a neutral glaze.
Garnish with one potato tuille and a pinch of fleur de sel.
notes: Ensure the potato puree is completely smooth to avoid lumps in the mousse.
The neutral glaze should be applied at exactly 32°C for optimal coverage.
Freeze the entremet completely before unmolding to maintain sharp edges.

recipes.recipe_name: Tom Kha Gai (Thai Coconut Chicken and Mushroom Soup)
recipes.visual_description: A deep, matte black ceramic bowl contains a creamy, ivory-white coconut broth. Large, succulent chunks of poached chicken thigh are nestled among halved grey oyster mushrooms and earthy straw mushrooms. The surface of the soup is dotted with vibrant red droplets of chili oil and bright green cilantro leaves. Thinly sliced rounds of red bird's eye chili and a single torn kaffir lime leaf provide contrast. The bowl sits on a rustic dark teak wood table next to a polished stainless steel Asian-style soup spoon and a folded charcoal grey linen napkin. A small side dish of lime wedges and fresh bird's eye chilies completes the authentic Thai setting. Natural side lighting highlights the silky texture of the broth.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a traditional ceramic tureen or individual deep bowls
Accompany with a side of steamed jasmine rice
Provide extra lime wedges and fish sauce on the side for personal seasoning

ingredients.name: Lemongrass, bruised and cut into 5cm lengths

instructions: Cut chicken into 3cm chunks.
Combine chicken stock, galangal, lemongrass, and kaffir lime leaves in a pot.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Add chicken chunks to the simmering broth.
Cook chicken until the internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Add oyster mushrooms and bruised chilies.
Simmer for 2 minutes until mushrooms soften.
Stir in coconut milk, fish sauce, and palm sugar.
Heat through but do not boil to prevent coconut milk from curdling.
Remove from heat and stir in fresh lime juice.
Discard lemongrass and galangal pieces before serving.
notes: Do not boil the soup after adding lime juice as it can turn bitter.
Galangal is essential for the authentic flavor and cannot be replaced by ginger.
Bruising the aromatics releases the essential oils for a deeper flavor profile.
traditional_techniques: balancing salty, sour, and creamy flavors

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Red Curry with Pork and Eggplant
recipes.visual_description: The Thai Red Curry is presented in a shallow, matte-finished ceramic bowl on a dark wood table. The dish features tender 3cm chunks of pork shoulder and 3cm wedges of eggplant, both glistening in a rich, orange-red coconut gravy. The pork chunks are piled naturally in the center, never sliced or fanned. The eggplant wedges are arranged around the meat, showing a soft, creamy texture. A thin layer of red chili oil floats on the surface, indicating authentic technique. Bright green Thai basil leaves and diagonal slices of red chili provide a fresh color contrast. A separate small bowl of white jasmine rice and a traditional ceramic spoon complete the professional casual dining setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice in a separate porcelain bowl
Provide a traditional Thai ceramic spoon and fork
Accompany with a side of Prik Nam Pla (fish sauce with chilies)
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Add red curry paste. Stir-fry for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in 100ml of coconut milk. Stir constantly until the oil separates from the cream.
Add pork chunks to the pot. Sear for 5 minutes until browned.
Add remaining coconut milk and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Lower heat. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add eggplant wedges. Simmer for 10 minutes until eggplant is tender.
Check pork internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Stir in fish sauce and palm sugar. Adjust seasoning to balance salt and sweet.
Add torn lime leaves and Thai basil. Remove from heat immediately.
notes: Do not peel the eggplant; the skin holds the wedges together during simmering
Ensure the coconut milk 'cracks' (separates) to develop the best flavor profile
Use pork shoulder for the best fat-to-meat ratio in slow-simmered curries

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Honey Plums with Aleppo Pepper Labneh
recipes.visual_description: A single portion served on a handcrafted, cream-colored ceramic plate with a matte texture. A thick, circular dollop of creamy white labneh sits slightly off-center, showing a smooth, dense texture. Three large, quartered plums, softened and glossy from fermentation, are nestled on the labneh. The plums exhibit a deep burgundy hue. A vibrant red-orange honey syrup, flecked with visible flakes of Aleppo pepper, is drizzled over the fruit and pools naturally around the labneh base. Toasted, grey-gold sunflower seeds are scattered on top. Tiny, vibrant green mint leaves are placed as a garnish. The lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the contrast between the white dairy and the dark fruit. The background features a textured light wood surface and a simple linen napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small glass of strong, unsweetened mint tea
Use traditional hand-thrown pottery bowls for service
Present as a light conclusion to a mezze-style meal
instructions: Line a sieve with cheesecloth. Place over a bowl.
Add yogurt and salt to the sieve. Drain in refrigerator for 12 hours.
Wash and quarter plums. Remove stones.
Whisk honey and Aleppo pepper in a glass jar.
Fold plums into the honey mixture. Ensure full coating.
Cover jar loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 48 hours until bubbly.
Store fermented plums in the refrigerator.
Toast sunflower seeds in a dry pan until golden. Cool completely.
Spoon 125 g of labneh onto each plate. Create a small well.
Place three plum quarters into the center. Drizzle with fermentation syrup.
Garnish with toasted seeds and torn mint leaves.
notes: Infuse plum pits into apple cider vinegar for a zero-waste shrub
Use local wildflower honey to support regional biodiversity
Save the whey from the yogurt to use in sourdough baking

recipes.recipe_name: Stir-Fried Napa Cabbage with Pork Belly and Fried Dough Twists
recipes.visual_description: A shallow, wide celadon ceramic bowl holds a vibrant heap of stir-fried elements. The hero ingredient, Napa cabbage, shows a mix of translucent, ivory-white stems and wilted, emerald-green leaves, both glistening with a savory soy glaze. Interspersed are golden-brown, irregular chunks of fried dough twists, their textured surfaces partially softened by the sauce. Thick 3cm squares of seared pork belly provide a rich, caramelized contrast. Purple onion wedges are softened but retain their shape. The dish is garnished with a scatter of fresh scallion rounds. The setting includes a pair of dark wood chopsticks on a rest, a small side dish of pickled garlic, and a clean linen napkin placed on a light oak table.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed white rice
Accompany with Laba garlic (vinegar-pickled garlic)
Pair with a light jasmine tea
instructions: Slice pork belly into 3cm squares, approximately 5mm thick.
Tear napa cabbage leaves into 5cm pieces, separating white stems from green leaves.
Slice red onion into 1cm wedges.
Break fried dough twists into 4cm irregular chunks.
Mince garlic and ginger finely.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Add pork belly squares. Render fat until meat is golden and edges are crisp.
Add onion wedges, garlic, ginger, and dried chilies. Stir-fry for 1 minute.
Increase heat to high. Add cabbage stems. Stir-fry for 2 minutes until slightly softened.
Add cabbage leaves. Stir-fry until just wilted.
Whisk light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, vinegar, and sugar in a small bowl.
Pour sauce over the vegetables.
Add fried dough twist chunks. Toss rapidly for 30 seconds to coat in sauce.
Garnish with sliced scallion rounds and serve immediately.
notes: Add the fried dough twists at the very end to maintain a slight crunch.
The dark soy sauce is primarily for a deep amber color.
High heat is essential for wok hei flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Braised Chicken with Roasted Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish braised chicken served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. Two whole bone-in chicken thighs with deep golden-brown skin sit at the center, partially submerged in a thick, vibrant red tomato and onion sofrito sauce. The sauce features softened 2cm carrot rounds and finely diced onions. Surrounding the chicken are several 3cm roasted potato wedges with crispy, browned edges. The dish is finished with a sprinkle of bright green chopped parsley. The setting is a dark wood bistro table with a side of crusty white bread. Lighting is natural and soft, highlighting the glossy texture of the sauce and the rustic arrangement.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty white bread to soak up the sofrito sauce
Pair with a glass of Tempranillo or light Spanish red wine
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family-style dining
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Season chicken generously with salt.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken pieces until skin is golden brown and crispy.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add remaining olive oil to the same pan.
Toss potato wedges with salt and roast on a baking sheet for 30 minutes until edges are crisp.
In the pan, sauté diced onions and carrot rounds for 8 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Stir for 1 minute.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Cook for 5 minutes until sauce thickens.
Return chicken to the pan. Add chicken stock.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 25 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure the chicken skin is well-seared before braising for maximum flavor.
Do not peel the potatoes for a more rustic, authentic texture.
The sauce should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.

recipes.recipe_name: Stir-Fried Napa Cabbage with Pork Belly and Fried Dough Twists
recipes.visual_description: A shallow, wide celadon ceramic bowl holds a vibrant heap of stir-fried elements. The hero ingredient, Napa cabbage, shows a mix of translucent, ivory-white stems and wilted, emerald-green leaves, both glistening with a savory soy glaze. Interspersed are golden-brown, irregular chunks of fried dough twists, their textured surfaces partially softened by the sauce. Thick 3cm squares of seared pork belly provide a rich, caramelized contrast. Purple onion wedges are softened but retain their shape. The dish is garnished with a scatter of fresh scallion rounds. The setting includes a pair of dark wood chopsticks on a rest, a small side dish of pickled garlic, and a clean linen napkin placed on a light oak table.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed white rice
Accompany with Laba garlic (vinegar-pickled garlic)
Pair with a light jasmine tea
instructions: Slice pork belly into 3cm squares, approximately 5mm thick.
Tear napa cabbage leaves into 5cm pieces, separating white stems from green leaves.
Slice red onion into 1cm wedges.
Break fried dough twists into 4cm irregular chunks.
Mince garlic and ginger finely.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Add pork belly squares. Render fat until meat is golden and edges are crisp.
Add onion wedges, garlic, ginger, and dried chilies. Stir-fry for 1 minute.

Whisk light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, vinegar, and sugar in a small bowl.
